excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: So it is right for you to keep pace with the bishop's mind, and you already do. Your presbytery, deservedly renowned and worthy of God, is tuned to the bishop like strings to a lyre. That is why Jesus Christ is sung in your concord and in your harmonious love.

Now each of you, one by one, become a choir, so that, in tune with one another in concord and taking your pitch from God in unity, you may sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father, so that he may both hear you and recognize, by the good you do, that you are members of his Son. It does you good, then, to live in blameless unity, so that you may always share in God.
notes: Harmony of bishop and presbytery as lyre.
greek: Ὅθεν πρέπει ὑμῖν συντρέχειν τῇ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου γνώμῃ, ὅπερ καὶ ποιεῖτε. τὸ γὰρ ἀξιονόμαστον ὑμῶν πρεσβυτέριον, τοῦ θεοῦ ἄξιον, οὕτως συνήρμοσται τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, ὡς χορδαὶ κιθάρᾳ. διὰ τοῦτο ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν καὶ συμφώνῳ ἀγάπῃ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ᾅδεται.

καὶ οἱ κατ’ ἄνδρα δὲ χορὸς γίνεσθε, ἵνα σύμφωνοι ὄντες ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ, χρῶμα θεοῦ λαβόντες ἐν ἑνότητι, ᾅδητε ἐν φωνῇ μιᾷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῷ πατρί, ἵνα ὑμῶν καὶ ἀκούσῃ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκῃ, δἰ ὦν εὖ πράσσετε, μέλη ὄντας τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ. χρήσιμον οὖν ἐστὶν ὑμᾶς ἐν ἀμώμῳ ἑνότητι εἶναι, ἵνα καὶ θεοῦ πάντοτε μετέχητε.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: In a short time I came to know your bishop with a closeness that was not human but spiritual. If that is true of me, how much more do I count you blessed, who are joined with him as the church is joined with Jesus Christ, and as Jesus Christ is joined with the Father, so that all things may sound together in unity?

Let no one be deceived. Anyone who is not within the altar goes without the bread of God. For if the prayer of one or two carries such power, how much more the prayer of the bishop and the whole church?

So whoever stays away from the assembly is already proud and has passed sentence on himself. For it is written, "God opposes the proud" (Proverbs 3:34; James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5). Let us be eager, then, not to oppose the bishop, so that we may be subject to God.
notes: Altar / church membership; unity with bishop.
greek: Εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἐν μικρῷ χρόνῳ τοιαύτην συνήθειαν ἔσχον πρὸς τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ὑμῶν, οὐκ ἀνθρωπίνην οὖσαν, ἀλλὰ πνευματικήν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς μακαρίζω τοὺς ἐγκεκραμένους οὕτως, ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, καὶ ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρί, ἵνα πάντα ἐν ἑνότητι σύμφωνα ᾖ;
μηδεὶς πλανάσθω: ἑὰν μή τις ᾖ ἐντὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, ὑστερεῖται τοῦ ἄρτου τοῦ θεοῦ. εἰ γὰρ ἑνὸς καὶ δευτέρου προσευχὴ τοσαύτην ἰσχὺν ἔχει, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ἥ τε τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ πάσης τῆς ἐκκλησίας;
ὁ οὖν μὴ ἐρχόμενος ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὗτος ἤδη ὑπερηφανεῖ καὶ ἑαυτὸν διέκρινεν. γέγραπται γάρ: Ὑπερηφάνοις ὁ θεὸς ἀντιτάσσεται, σπουδάσωμεν οὖν μὴ ἀντιτάσσεσθαι τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ, ἵνα ὦμεν θεῷ ὑποτασσόμενοι.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: The more anyone sees a bishop keeping silent, the more let him stand in awe of him. Whoever the Master of the house sends to run his household, we must welcome as we would welcome the one who sent him (Matthew 10:40; John 13:20). Plainly, then, we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself.

Onesimus himself warmly praises your good order in God. You all live by the truth, and no faction makes its home among you. In fact, you do not even listen to anyone more than to one who speaks truly about Jesus Christ.
greek: Καὶ ὅσον βλέπει τις σιγῶντα ἐπίσκοπον, πλειόνως αὐτὸν φοβείσθω: πάντα γάρ, ὃν πέμπει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἰς ἰδίαν οἰκονομίαν, οὕτως δεῖ ἡμᾶς αὐτὸν δέχεσθαι, ὡς αὐτὸν τὸν πέμψαντα, τὸν οὖν ἐπίσκοπον δῆλον ὅτι ὡς αὐτὸν κύριον δεῖ προσβλέπειν.

αὐτὸς μὲν οὖν Ὀνήσιμος ὑπερεπαινεῖ ὑμῶν τὴν ἐν θεῷ εὐταξίαν, ὅτι πάντες κατὰ ἀλήθειαν ζῆτε καὶ ὅτι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐδεμία αἵρεσις κατοικεῖ: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἀκούετέ τινος πλέον, ἢ περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ λαλοῦντος ἐν ἀληθείᾳ.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: So make every effort to meet more often to give thanks to God and to give him glory. When you gather often, Satan's powers are torn down, and the ruin he works comes apart in the oneness of your faith.
Nothing is better than peace. In peace every war of heavenly beings and earthly beings is abolished.
notes: Frequent gathering for eucharist/thanksgiving and glory.
greek: Σπουδάζετε οὖν πυκνότερον συνέρχεσθαι εἰς εὐχαριστίαν θεοῦ καὶ εἰς δόξαν. ὅταν γὰρ πυκνῶς ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ γίνεσθε, καθαιροῦνται αἱ δυνάμεις τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ λύεται ὁ ὄλεθρος αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁμονοίᾳ ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως.
οὐδέν ἐστιν ἄμεινον εἰρήνης, ἐν ᾗ πᾶς πόλεμος καταργεῖται ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: So I have been granted the privilege of seeing you, through Damas, your bishop, a man worthy of God; through your worthy presbyters, Bassus and Apollonius; and through my fellow slave Zotion, the deacon. May I have joy in him! For he is subject to the bishop as to God's grace, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ.
greek: Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἠξιώθην ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς διὰ Δαμᾶ τοῦ ἀξιοθέου ὑμῶν ἐπισκόπου καὶ πρεσβυτέρων ἀξϊων Βάσσου καὶ Ἀπολλωνίου καὶ τοῦ συνδούλου μου διακόνου Ζωτίωνος, οὗ ἐγὼ ὀναίμην, ὅτι ὑποτάσσεται τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ὡς χάριτι θεοῦ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς νόμῳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: You too must not presume on your bishop's youth. According to the power of God the Father, render him every mark of respect. I know that the holy presbyters also have not presumed on his rank, young as it appears. As men wise in God they defer to him; not to him, though, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the Bishop of all.

To honor the One who has desired us, then, it is fitting to obey without any pretense. For a man does not deceive this bishop who is seen; he cheats the Bishop who is unseen. In such a case the reckoning is not with flesh but with God, who knows what is hidden.
greek: Καὶ ὑμῖν δὲ πρέπει μὴ συγχρᾶσθαι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου, ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν θεοῦ πατρὸς πᾶσαν ἐντροπὴν αὐτῷ ἀπονέμειν, καθὼς ἔγνων καὶ τοὺς ἁγίους πρεσβυτέρους οὐ προσειληφότας τὴν φαινομένην νεωτερικὴν τάξιν, ἀλλ’ ὡς φρονίμους ἐν θεῷ συγχωροῦντας αὐτῷ, οὐκ αὐτῷ δέ, ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τῷ πάντων ἐπισκόπῳ.

εἰς τιμὴν οὖν ἐκείνου τοῦ θελήσαντος ἡμᾶς πρέπον ἐστὶν ἐπακούειν κατὰ μηδεμίαν ὑπόκρισιν: ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὅτι τὸν ἐπίσκοπον τοῦτον τὸν βλεπόμενον πλανᾷ τις, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀόρατον παραλογίζεται. τὸ δὲ τοιοῦτον οὐ πρὸς σάρκα ὁ λόγος, ἀλλὰ πρὸς θεὸν τὸν τὰ κρύφια εἰδότα.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: It is fitting, then, not only to bear the name of Christians but to be Christians, just as some do call a man bishop, yet do everything without him. Such people do not seem to me to have a clean conscience, for they do not gather validly, as the commandment requires.
notes: Calling bishop while acting apart from him.
greek: Πρέπον οὖν ἐστιν μὴ μόνον καλεῖσθαι Χρις τιανούς, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἶναι: ὥσπερ καί τινες ἐπίσκοπον μὲν καλοῦσιν, χωρὶς δὲ αὐτοῦ πάντα πράσσουσιν. οἱ τοιοῦτοι δὲ οὐκ εὐσυνείδητοί μοι εἶναι φαίνονται διὰ τὸ μὴ βεβαίως κατ’ ἐντολὴν συναθροίζεσθαι.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: In the persons I have named I have looked on your whole congregation in faith, and I have loved it. So I urge you: be eager to do everything in God's own harmony, with the bishop presiding in the place of God, the presbyters in the place of the council of the apostles, and the deacons, so very dear to me, entrusted with the ministry of Jesus Christ, who was with the Father before the ages and at the end was revealed.

All of you, then, having received God's own character, respect one another. Let no one regard his neighbor according to the flesh; love one another in Jesus Christ, always. Let nothing be among you that could divide you. Be one with the bishop and with those who preside, as a pattern and a lesson of incorruption.
notes: Bishop in place of God; presbyters as apostolic council; deacons.
greek: Ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐν τοῖς προγεγραμμένοις προσώποις τὸ πᾶν πλῆθος ἐθεώρησα ἐν πίστει καὶ ἠγάπησα, παραινῶ, ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ θεοῦ σπουδάζετε πάντα πράσσειν, προκαθημένου τοῦ ἐπισκόπου εἰς τόπον θεοῦ καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων εἰς τόπον συνεδρίου τῶν ἀποστόλων, καὶ τῶν διακόνων τῶν ἐμοὶ γλυκυτάτων πεπιστευμένων διακονίαν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δς πρὸ αἰώνων παρὰ πατρὶ ἦν καὶ ἐν τέλει ἐφάνη.

πάντες οὖν ὁμοήθειαν θεοῦ λαβόντες ἐντρέπεσθε ἀλλήλους καὶ μηδεὶς κατὰ σάρκα βλεπέτω τὸν πλησίον, ἀλλ’ ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ ἀλλήλους διὰ παντὸς ἀγαπᾶτε. μηδὲν ἔστω ἐν ὑμῖν, ὃ δυνήσεται ὑμᾶς μερίσαι ἀλλ’ ἑνώθητε τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τοῖς προκαθημένοις εἰς τύπον καὶ διδαχὴν ἀφθαρσίας.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: The Lord was one with the Father and did nothing without him (John 5:19): nothing on his own, nothing through the apostles. In the same way, you must do nothing without the bishop and the presbyters. Do not try to make some private course look reasonable to yourselves. Come together in one place: one prayer, one plea, one mind, one hope, in love, in spotless joy. That joy is Jesus Christ, and nothing is better than he.
Run together, all of you, as to one temple of God, as to one altar, to one Jesus Christ. He came forth from one Father; he is with that One; and to that One he has returned.
notes: One prayer, one mind, one hope; nothing without bishop and presbyters.
greek: Ὥσπερ οὖν ὁ κύριος ἄνευ τοῦ πατρὸς οὐδὲν ἐποίησεν, ἡνωμένος ὤν, οὔτε δἰ ἑαυτοῦ οὔτε διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων: οὕτως μηδὲ ὑμεῖς ἄνευ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων μηδὲν πράσσετε: μηδὲ πειράσητε εὔλογόν τι φαίνεσθαι ἰδίᾳ ὑμῖν, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ μία προσευχή, μία δέησις, εἷς νοῦς, μία ἐλπὶς ἐν ἀγάπῃ, ἐν τῇ χαρᾷ τῇ ἀμώμῳ, ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, οὖ ἄμεινον οὐδέν ἐστιν.
πάντες ὡς εἰς ἕνα ναὸν συντρέχετε θεοῦ, ὡς ἐπὶ ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ἐπὶ ἕνα Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν ἀφ̓ ἑνὸς πατρὸς προελθόντα καὶ εἰς ἕνα ὄντα καὶ χωρήσαντα.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: If, then, those who had lived under the old order of things came to a new hope, no longer keeping the Sabbath but living according to the Lord's day, the day on which our life also dawned through him and through his death (which some deny, through that mystery we received faith, and for this reason we endure, so that we may be found disciples of Jesus Christ, our only Teacher), how shall we be able to live apart from him?
Even the prophets were his disciples in the Spirit, and they looked for him as their Teacher. And for this reason the One they rightly awaited, when he came, raised them from the dead.
notes: Living according to the Lord’s day rather than sabbatizing.
greek: Εἰ οὖν οἱ ἐν παλαιοῖς πράγμασιν ἀναστραφέντες εἰς καινότητα ἐλπίδος ἦλθον, μηκέτι σαββατίζοντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ κυριακὴν ζῶντες, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἡμῶν ἀνέτειλεν δἰ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, ὅν τινες ἀρνοῦνται, δἰ οὗ μυστηρίου ἐλάβομεν τὸ πιστεύειν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ὑπομένομεν, ἵνα εὑρεθῶμεν μαθηταὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ μόνου διδασκάλου ἡμῶν:
πῶς ἡμεῖς δυνησόμεθα ζῆσαι χωρὶς αὐτοῦ, οὗ καὶ οἱ προφῆται μαθηταὶ ὄντες τῷ πνεύματι ὡς διδάσκαλον αὐτὸν προσεδόκων; καὶ διὰ τοῦτο, ὃν δικαίως ἀνέμενον, παρὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτοὺς ἐκ νεκρῶν.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: Strive, then, to be established in the teachings of the Lord and of the apostles, so that you may prosper in all you do: in flesh and in spirit, in faith and in love, in the Son and the Father and the Spirit, at the beginning and at the end. May you prosper together with your bishop, most worthy of honor, with your presbytery, that finely woven spiritual crown, and with your godly deacons.
Submit to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ submitted to the Father, and as the apostles submitted to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a union of flesh and of spirit alike.
greek: Σπουδάζετε οὖν βεβαιωθῆναι ἐν τοῖς δόγμασιν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων, ἵνα πάντα, ὅσα ποιεῖτε, κατευοδωθῆτε σαρκὶ καὶ πνεύματι, πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ, ἐν υἱῷ καὶ πατρὶ καὶ ἐν πνεύματι, ἐν ἀρχῇ καὶ ἐν τέλει, μετὰ τοῦ ἀξιοπρεπεστάτου ἐπισκόπου ὑμῶν καὶ ἀξιοπλόκου πνευματικοῦ στεφάνου τοῦ πρεσβυτερίου ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν κατὰ θεὸν διακόνων.
ὑποτάγητε τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ ἀλλήλοις, ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρὶ καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῷ πατρὶ ἵνα ἕνωσις ᾖ σαρκική τε καὶ πνευματική.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: When you submit to the bishop as you would to Jesus Christ, I can see that you are not living by human standards. You live by Jesus Christ, who died for us so that, believing in his death, you might escape death.

So it is necessary, and you already do it, that you undertake nothing apart from the bishop. Submit also to the presbytery as to the apostles of Jesus Christ, our hope. If we make our life in him, in him we will be found.

The deacons, too, serve the mysteries of Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 4:1), and they must please everyone in every way. They are not waiters handing round food and drink; they are servants of God's church. So they must shun every charge against them as they would shun fire.
greek: Ὅταν γὰρ τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ὑποτάσσησθε ὡς Ἱησοῦ Χριστῷ, φαίνεσθέ μοι οὐ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ζῶντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν δἰ ἡμᾶς ἀποθανόντα, ἵνα πιστεύσαντες εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτοῦ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν ἐκφύγητε.
ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἐστίν, ὥσπερ ποιεῖτε, ἄνευ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μηδὲν πράσσειν ὑμᾶς, ἀλλ’ ὑποτάσσεσθαι καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς τοῖς ἀποστόλοις Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῆς ἐλπίδος ἡμῶν, ἐν ᾦ διάγοντες εὑρεθησόμεθα.

δεῖ δὲ καὶ τοὺς διακόνους ὄντας μυστηρίων Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ κατὰ πάντα τρόπον πᾶσιν ἀρέσκειν. οὐ γὰρ βρωμάτων καὶ ποτῶν εἰσιν διάκονοι, ἀλλ’ ἐκκλησίας θεοῦ ὑπηρέται: δέον οὖν αὐτοὺς φυλάσσεσθαι τὰ ἐγκλήματα ὡς πῦρ.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: Likewise, let everyone honor the deacons as Jesus Christ, and the bishop too, for he is a figure of the Father, and the presbyters as God's council and the apostles' band. Without these, nothing is called a church.

I am sure you feel the same about all this. For I have received the sample of your love, and I keep it with me in your bishop. His very bearing is a great lesson, and his gentleness is power. I think even the godless honor him.
Because I love you, I spare you, though I could write more sharply on this point. I did not think myself fit for this, that I, a condemned man, should issue you commands like an apostle.
notes: Without these the church is not called.
greek: Ὁμοίως πάντες ἐντρεπέσθωσαν τοὺς διακόνους ὡς Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ὡς καὶ τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ὄντα τύπον τοῦ πατρός. τοὺς δὲ πρεσβυτέρους ὡς συνέδριον θεοῦ καὶ ὡς σύνδεσμον ἀποστόλων. χωρὶς τούτων ἐκκλησία οὐ καλεῖται.

περὶ ὧν πέπεισμαι ὑμᾶς οὕτως ἔχειν. τὸ γὰρ ἐξεμπλάριον τῆς ἀγάπης ὑμῶν ἔλαβον καὶ ἔχω μεθ̓ ἑαυτοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ὑμῶν, οὖ αὐτὸ τὸ κατάστημα μεγάλη μαθητεία, ἡ δὲ πραότης αὐτοῦ δύναμις: ὃν λογίζομαι καὶ τοὺς ἀθέους ἐντρέπεσθαι.
ἀγαπῶν ὑμᾶς φείδομαι, συντονώτερον δυνάμενος γράφειν ὑπὲρ τούτου. οὐκ εἰς τοῦτο ᾠήθην, ἵνα ὤν κατάκριτος ὡς ἀπόστολος ὑμῖν διατάσσωμαι.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: So I urge you, or rather not I, but the love of Jesus Christ urges you: eat only Christian food, and keep clear of every foreign plant. That plant is heresy.

Such people blend Jesus Christ in with themselves, putting on a show of trustworthiness. They are like poisoners who serve a deadly drug in sweet wine. The one who does not know drinks it down with pleasure, and with that evil pleasure swallows his own death.
greek: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, οὐκ ἐγώ, ἀλλ’ ἡ ἀγάπη Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: μόνῃ τῇ χριστιανῇ τροφῇ χρῆσθε, ἀλλοτρίας δὲ βοτάνης ἀπέχεσθε, ἥτις ἐστὶν αἵρεσις:
οἳ ἑαυτοῖς παρεμπλέκουσιν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν καταξιοπιστευόμενοι, ὥσπερ θανάσιμον φάρμακον διδόντες μετὰ οἰνομέλιτος, ὅπερ ὁ ἀγνοῶν ἡδέως λαμβάνει ἐν ἡδονῇ κακῇ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: So be on your guard against such people. And this will hold true for you if you are not puffed up with pride, and if you stay inseparable from God, Jesus Christ, and from the bishop and the commands of the apostles.

Whoever is inside the altar's sanctuary is clean; whoever is outside the sanctuary is not clean. That is, whoever does anything apart from the bishop, the presbytery, and the deacons does not have a clean conscience.
notes: Inside/outside the altar = with/without bishop, presbytery, deacons.
greek: Φυλάττεσθε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους. τοῦτο δὲ ἔσται ὑμῖν μὴ φυσιουμένοις καὶ οὖσιν ἀχωρίστοις θεοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου καὶ τῶν διαταγμάτων τῶν ἀποστόλων.
ὁ ἐντὸς θυσιαστηρίου ὢν καθαρός ἐστιν: ὁ δὲ ἐκτὸς θυσιαστηρίου ὤν οὐ καθαρός ἐστιν. τοῦτ̓ ἔστιν, ὁ χωρὶς ἐπισκόπου καὶ πρεσβυτερίου καὶ διακόνων πράσσων τι, οὗτος οὐ καθαρός ἐστιν τῇ συνειδήσει.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: You are children of the light of truth (Ephesians 5:8), so run from division and from evil teaching. Wherever the shepherd is, be there, following like sheep. Many wolves wear a trustworthy face, and with wicked pleasure they carry off as captives those who are running toward God. But in your unity they will have no room.
greek: Τέκνα οὖν φωτὸς ἀληθείας, φεύγετε τὸν μερισμὸν καὶ τὰς κακοδιδασκαλίας: ὅπου δὲ ὁ ποιμήν ἐστιν, ἐκεῖ ὡς πρόβατα ἀκολουθεῖτε.
πολλοὶ γὰρ λύκοι ἀξιόπιστοι ἡδονῇ κακῇ αἰχμαλωτίζουσιν τοὺς θεοδρόμους: ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ ἑνότητι ὑμῶν οὐχ ἕξουσιν τόπον.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: Stay clear of the bad weeds. Jesus Christ does not tend them, for they are not the Father's planting (Matthew 15:13). Not that I found division among you; I found a sifting.
All who are God's and Jesus Christ's are with the bishop. And all who repent and enter the unity of the church will be God's too, so that they may live according to Jesus Christ.

Do not be deceived, my brothers: if anyone follows a man who splits the church, he does not inherit the kingdom of God (1 Corinthians 6:9–10). If anyone walks in an alien mind, he does not consent to the Passion.
notes: Those of God are with the bishop; repentance unto unity of the church.
greek: Ἀπέχεσθε τῶν κακῶν βοτανῶν, ἅστινας οὐ γεωργεῖ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι αὐτοὺς φυτείαν πατρός: οὐχ ὅτι παῤ ὑμῖν μερισμὸν εὗρον, ἀλλ’ ὰποδιῡλισμόν.
ὅσοι γὰρ θεοῦ εἰσιν καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὗτοι μετὰ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου εἰσίν. καὶ ὅσοι ἂν μετανοήσαντες ἔλθωσιν ἐπὶ τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς ἐκκλησίας, καὶ οὗτοι θεοῦ ἔσονται, ἵνα ὦσιν κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ζῶντες.
μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου: εἴ τις σχίζοντι ἀκολουθεῖ. βασιλείαν θεοῦ οὐ κληρονομεῖ: εἴ τις ἐν ἀλλοτρίᾳ γνώμῃ περιπατεῖ, οὗτος τῷ πάθει οὐ συγκατατίθεται.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: Be eager, then, to use one Eucharist, so that whatever you do, you do it God's way. For there is one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ, and one cup for union with his blood. There is one altar, just as there is one bishop, with the presbytery and the deacons, my fellow slaves.
notes: One eucharist, one flesh, one cup, one altar, one bishop.
greek: Σπουδάσατε οὖν μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι: μία γὰρ σὰρξ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἓν ποτήριον εἰς ἕνωσιν τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ὡς εἷς ἐπίσκοπος ἅμα τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις τοῖς συνδούλοις μου: ἵνα, ὃ ἐὰν πράσσητε, κατὰ θεὸν πράσσητε.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh, the Spirit is not deceived, for it is from God. It knows where it comes from and where it is going (John 3:8), and it lays bare what is hidden. While I was with you I cried out; I spoke with a loud voice, God's own voice: "Pay attention to the bishop, to the presbytery, and to the deacons."

Some suspected that I said this because I already knew of the split among certain people. But the One in whom I am bound is my witness that I did not learn it from human flesh. The Spirit was preaching, saying this: "Do nothing without the bishop. Guard your flesh as God's temple. Love unity. Run from divisions. Become imitators of Jesus Christ, as he is of his Father (1 Corinthians 11:1)."
notes: Spirit cried: attend to bishop, presbytery, deacons.
greek: Εἰ γὰρ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα μέ τινες ἠθέλησαν πλανῆσαι, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα οὐ πλανᾶται ἀπὸ θεοῦ ὄν. οἶδεν γάρ, πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει, καὶ τὰ κρυπτὰ ἐλέγχει. ἐκραύγασα μεταξὺ ὤν, ἐλάλουν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ, θεοῦ φωνῇ: Τῷ ἐπισκοπῳ προσέχετε καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις.

οἱ δὲ ὑποπτεύσαντές με ὡς προειδότα τὸν μερισμόν τινων λέγειν ταῦτα: μάρτυς δέ μοι, ἐν ᾧ δέδεμαι, ὅτι ἀπὸ σαρκὸς ἀνθρωπίνης οὐκ ἔγνων. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐκήρυσσεν λέγον τάδε: Χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μηδὲν ποιεῖτε, τὴν σάρκα ὑμῶν ὡς ναὸν θεοῦ τηρεῖτε, τὴν ἕνωσιν ἀγαπᾶτε, τοὺς μερισμοὺς φεύγετε, μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: I, then, was doing my part, as a man fitted for unity. Where there is division and anger, God does not dwell. To all who repent the Lord grants forgiveness, if in repenting they turn to the unity of God and to the bishop's council. I trust in the grace of Jesus Christ, who will loose every chain from you.

Here is my plea: act from no spirit of rivalry (Philippians 2:3), but as those taught by Christ. For I heard some people saying, "Unless I find it in the archives, I don't believe it in the gospel." I told them, "It is written." Their reply: "That is exactly what is in dispute." But my archives are Jesus Christ. His cross, his death, his resurrection, and the faith that comes through him: these are the archives no one can tamper with. By these, through your prayer, I long to be justified.
notes: Forgiveness for those who repent into God’s unity and the bishop’s council.
greek: Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν τὸ ἴδιον ἐποίουν ὡς ἄνθρωπος εἰς ἕνωσιν κατηρτισμένος. οὗ δὲ μερισμός ἐστιν καὶ ὀργή. θεὸς οὐ κατοικεῖ. πᾶσιν οὖν μετανοοῦσιν ἀφίει ὁ κύριος, ἐὰν μετανοήσωσιν εἰς ἑνότητα θεοῦ καὶ συνέδριον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου. πιστεύω τῇ χάριτι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς λύσει ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν πάντα δεσμόν.

παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς μηδὲν κατ’ ἐριθείαν πράσσειν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ χριστομαθίαν. ἐπεὶ ἤκουσά τινων λεγόντων, ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ ἐν τοῖς ἀρχείοις εὕρω ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ οὐ πιστεύω: καὶ λέγοντός μου αὐτοῖς ὅτι γέγραπται, ἀπεκρίθησάν μοι ὅτι πρόκειται. ἐμοὶ δὲ ἀρχεῖά ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὰ ἄθικτα ἀρχεῖα ὁ σταυρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ πίστις ἡ δἰ αὐτοῦ, ἐν οἶς θέλω ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν δικαιωθῆναι.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: They stay away from the Eucharist and from prayer, because they will not confess that the Eucharist is the flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ. That flesh suffered for our sins. That flesh the Father in his kindness raised. Those who argue against God's gift die arguing. They would do better to love, so that they too might rise.

So it is right to stay clear of such people and not talk about them, privately or publicly. Give your attention to the prophets, and above all to the gospel. There the passion has been shown to us, and the resurrection made complete. Run from divisions. They are where evil begins.
notes: Heterodox abstain from eucharist/prayer; refuse to confess eucharist as flesh of Savior.
greek: Εὐχαριστίας καὶ πρυσευχῆς ἀπέχονται, διὰ τὸ μὴ ὁμολογεῖν τὴν εὐχαριστίαν σάρκα εἶναι τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν παθοῦσαν, ἣν τῇ χρηστότητι ὁ πατὴρ ἤγειρεν. οἱ οὖν ἀντιλέγοντες τῇ δωρεᾷ τοῦ θεοῦ συζητοῦντες ἀποθνήσκουσιν: συνέφερεν δε αὐτοῖς ἀγαπᾶν, ἵνα καὶ ἀναστῶσιν.

πρέπον ἐστὶν ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν τοιούτων καὶ μήτε κατ’ ἰδίαν περὶ αὐτῶν λαλεῖν μήτε κοινῇ, προσέχειν δὲ τοῖς προφήταις, ἐξαιρέτως δὲ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ, ἐν ᾧ τὸ πάθος ἡμῖν δεδήλωται καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις τετελείωται. τοὺς δὲ μερισμοὺς φεύγετε ὡς ἀρχὴν κακῶν.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: Every one of you, follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ follows the Father. Follow the presbytery as you would the apostles. Honor the deacons as you would God's own command. Let no one do anything that belongs to the church without the bishop. Let that Eucharist be held valid which is under the bishop, or under someone he has entrusted with it.

Where the bishop appears, there let the people be, just as where Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic church. Without the bishop it is not permitted either to baptize or to hold the love feast. But whatever he approves is pleasing to God as well, so that everything you do may be sure and valid.
notes: Valid eucharist under bishop; baptism and love-feast only with bishop.
greek: Πάντες τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ἀκολουθεῖτε, ὡς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τῷ πατρί, καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ὡς τοῖς ἀποστόλοις. τοὺς δὲ διακόνους ἐντρέπεσθε ὡς θεοῦ ἐντολήν. μηδεὶς χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου τι πρασσέτω τῶν ἀνηκόντων εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν. ἐκείνη βεβαία εὐχαριστία ἡγείσθω, ἡ ὑπὸ ἐπίσκοπον οὖσα ἢ ᾧ ἄν αὐτὸς ἐπιτρέψῃ.

ὅπου ἂν φανῇ ὁ ἐπίσκοπος, ἐκεῖ τὸ πλῆθος ἤτω, ὥσπερ ὅπου ἂν ᾖ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, ἐκεῖ ἡ καθολικὴ ἐκκλησία. οὐκ ἐξόν ἐστιν χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου οὔτε βαπτίζειν οὔτε ἀγάπην ποιεῖν: ἀλλ’ ὃ ἂν ἐκεῖνος δοκιμάσῃ, τοῦτο καὶ τῷ θεῷ εὐάρεστον, ἵνα ἀσφαλὲς ᾖ καὶ βέβαιον πᾶν ὃ πράσσετε.

excerpts.author: Ignatius of Antioch
english: It is reasonable, from now on, that we come to our senses, while we still have time to repent and turn to God. It is good to know God and the bishop. Whoever honors the bishop has been honored by God. Whoever does anything behind the bishop's back is serving the devil.

So let everything overflow for you in grace, for you are worthy. You have given me rest in every way; may Jesus Christ give you rest. You loved me when I was away and when I was with you. God is your reward. Enduring all things for his sake, you will reach him.
greek: Εὔλογόν ἐστιν λοιπὸν ἀνανῆψαι ἡμᾶς, ὡς ἔτι καιρὸν ἔχομεν εἰς θεὸν μετανοεῖν. καλῶς ἔχει, θεὸν καὶ ἐπίσκοπον εἰδέναι. ὁ τιμῶν ἐπίσκοπον ὑπὸ θεοῦ τετίμηται: ὁ λάθρα ἐπισκόπου τι πράσσων τῷ διαβόλῳ λατρεύει.
πάντα οὖν ὑμῖν ἐν χάριτι περισσευέτω: ἄξιοι γάρ ἐστε. κατὰ πάντα με ἀνεπαύσατε, καὶ ὑμᾶς Ἰησοῦς Χριστός. ἀπόντα με καὶ πάροντα ἠγαπήσατε. ἀμοιβὴ ὑμῖν ὁ θεός, δἰ ὃν πάντα ὑπομένοντες αὐτοῦ τεύξεσθε.

excerpts.author: Polycarp of Smyrna
english: Since we know that God is not mocked (Galatians 6:7), we ought to live in a way worthy of his commandment and his glory.

The deacons, too, must be blameless before his righteousness, as deacons of God and Christ and not of people. They must not be slanderers or two-faced (1 Timothy 3:8), not greedy for money, but self-controlled in everything, compassionate, and diligent, walking by the truth of the Lord, who became the servant of all (Mark 9:35). If we please him in this present age, we will receive the age to come as well, just as he promised to raise us from the dead, and that if we live as citizens worthy of him, we will also reign with him (2 Timothy 2:12), if indeed we believe.

The young men, likewise, must be blameless in everything, taking thought above all for purity and reining themselves in from every evil. It is good to be cut off from the cravings of this world, because every craving wages war against the Spirit (1 Peter 2:11), and neither the sexually immoral, nor men who submit to homosexual acts, nor men who commit them will inherit the kingdom of God (1 Corinthians 6:9–10), nor will those who do vile things. So we must keep away from all of this and submit to the presbyters and deacons as to God and Christ. The virgins must walk with a blameless and pure conscience.
greek: Εἰδότες, οὖν, ὅτι θεὸς οὐ μυκτηρίζεται, ὀφείλομεν ἀξίως τῆς ἐντολῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ δόξης περιπατεῖν.

ὁμοίως διάκονοι ἄμεμπτοι κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὡς θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ διάκονοι καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπων: μὴ διάβολοι, μὴ δίλογοι, ἀφιλάργυροι, ἐγκρατεῖς περὶ πάντα, εὔσπλαγχνοι, ἐπιμελεῖς, πορευόμενοι κατὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ κυρίου, ὃς ἐγένετο διάκονος πάντων: ᾧ ἐὰν εὐαρεστήσωμεν ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι, ἀποληψόμεθα καὶ τὸν μέλλοντα, καθὼς ὑπέσχετο ἡμῖν ἐγεῖραι ἡμᾶς ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ ὅτι ἐὰν πολιτευσώμεθα ἀξίως αὐτοῦ, καὶ συμβασιλεύσομεν αὐτῷ, εἴγε πιστεύομεν.

ὁμοίως καὶ νεώτεροι ἄμεμπτοι ἐν πᾶσιν, πρὸ παντὸς προνοοῦντες ἁγνείας καὶ χαλιναγωγοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ παντὸς κακοῦ. καλὸν γὰρ τὸ ἀνακόπτεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, ὅτι πᾶσα ἐπιθυμία κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος στρατεύεται, καὶ οὔτε πόρνοι οὔτε μαλακοὶ οὔτε ἀρσενοκοῖται βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομήσουσιν, οὔτε οἱ ποιοῦντες τὰ ἄτοπα. διὸ δέον ἀπέχεσθαι ἀπὸ πάντων τούτων, ὑποτασσομένους τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις καὶ διακόνοις ὡς θεῷ καὶ Χριστῷ: τὰς παρθένους ἐν ἀμώμῳ καὶ ἁγνῇ συνειδήσει περιπατεῖν.

excerpts.author: Polycarp of Smyrna
english: The presbyters, for their part, must be tenderhearted and merciful to everyone. They should bring back those who have wandered, visit all who are sick, and never neglect a widow, an orphan, or anyone poor, but always take thought for what is good in the sight of God and people (Proverbs 3:4; 2 Corinthians 8:21). Let them keep clear of all anger, favoritism, and unjust judgment, and stay far from every love of money. They must not be quick to believe an accusation against anyone or harsh in judging, knowing that we are all in debt to sin.

If, then, we ask the Lord to forgive us, we too must forgive (Matthew 6:12, 14), for we are before the eyes of the Lord and God, and all of us must stand before the judgment seat of Christ, and each must give an account of himself (Romans 14:10, 12).

So let us serve him with fear and all reverence (Hebrews 12:28), just as he himself commanded, and the apostles who brought us the gospel, and the prophets who foretold our Lord's coming. Let us be zealous for what is good, and keep away from stumbling blocks, from false brothers, and from those who bear the name of the Lord in hypocrisy, who lead empty people astray.
notes: Attend to bishop; baptism mentioned in household duties context — primarily order.
greek: Καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι δὲ εὔσπλαγχνοι, εἰς πάντας ἐλεήμονες, ἐπιστρέφοντες τὰ ἀποπεπλανημένα, ἐπισκεπτόμενοι πάντας ἀσθενεῖς, μὴ ἀμελοῦντες χήρας ἢ ὀρφανοῦ ἢ πένητος ἀλλὰ προνοοῦντες ἀεὶ τοῦ καλοῦ ἐνώπιον θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων, ἀπεχόμενοι πάσης ὀργῆς, προσωποληψίας, κρίσεως ἀδίκου, μακρὰν ὄντες πάσης φιλαργυρίας, μὴ ταχέως πιστεύοντες κατά τινος, μὴ ἀπότομοι ἐν κρίσει, εἰδότες ὅτι πάντες ὀφειλέται ἐσμὲν ἁμαρτίας.

εἰ οὖν δεόμεθα τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα ἡμῖν ἀφῇ, ὀφείλομεν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφιέναι: ἀπέναντι γὰρ τῶν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ θεοῦ ἐσμὲν ὀφθαλμῶν, καὶ πάντας δεῖ παραστῆναι τῷ βήματι τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἕκαστον ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ λόγον δοῦναι.

οὕτως οὖν δουλεύσωμεν αὐτῷ μετὰ φόβου καὶ πάσης εὐλαβείας, καθὼς αὐτὸς ἐνετείλατο καὶ οἱ εὐαγγελισάμενοι ἡμᾶς ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ προφῆται, οἱ προκηρύξαντες τὴν ἔλευσιν τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν: ζηλωταὶ περὶ τὸ καλόν, ἀπεχόμενοι τῶν σκανδάλων καὶ τῶν ψευδαδέλφων καὶ τῶν ἐν ὑποκρίσει φερόντων τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίον, οἵτινες ἀποπλανῶσι κενοὺς ἀνθρώπους.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 1
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: The Lord warns us: "You are the salt of the earth" (Matt. 5:13). He commands us to be innocent as doves, yet prudent as serpents. What else, dearest brothers, should we do but look ahead and stay alert, with anxious hearts, so that we both grasp and guard against the snares of our cunning enemy? We have put on Christ, the wisdom of God the Father; we must not appear less wise in protecting our salvation. Persecution is not the only danger, nor only those open attacks that rage against God's servants to overthrow and cast them down. Caution comes easily when the threat is obvious, and the mind readies itself for battle when the adversary shows himself. The enemy is far more to be feared and avoided when he creeps up secretly, deceiving under the guise of peace and slipping in by hidden approaches—that is why he is called the serpent. Such is his constant cunning, the blind and hidden deceit he uses to entrap human beings. From the very beginning of the world he deceived, coaxing inexperienced souls with lying words and catching them in their unguarded credulity. He even attempted to tempt the Lord Himself, stealing in again as if to deceive once more. Yet he was recognized and repulsed, and so he was thrown down, because he was identified and exposed.
notes: Opening: stay in the church; schism danger.
latin: CUM moneat Dominus et dicat: Vos estis sal terrae, cumque esse nos jubeat ad innocentiam simplices, et tamen cum simplicitate prudentes, quid aliud, fratres dilectissimi, quam providere nos convenit, et sollicito corde vigilantes, subdoli hostis insidias intelligere pariter et cavere ne qui Christum sapientiam Dei Patris induimus, minus sapere in tuenda salute videamur? Neque enim persecutio sola metuenda est et ea quae subruendis ac dejiciendis Dei servis aperta impugnatione grassantur. Facilior cautio est ubi manifesta formido est, et ad certamen animus ante praestruitur quando se adversarius confitetur. Plus metuendus est et cavendus inimicus cum latenter obrepit, cum, per pacis imaginem fallens, occultis accessibus serpit; unde et nomen serpentis accepit. Ea est ejus semper astutia, ea est circumveniendi hominis caeca et latebrosa fallacia. Sic ab initio statim mundi fefellit, et, verbis mendacibus blandiens, rudes animas incauta credulitate decepit. Dominum ipsum tentare conatus, quasi obreperet rursus et falleret, latenter accessit. Intellectus tamen est et retusus; et ideo prostratus, quia agnitus atque detectus.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 3
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: My dearest brothers, we must guard ourselves not only against open and obvious dangers but also against those that deceive through the subtle cunning of fraud. For what could be more cunning, what more subtle, than this: the enemy, exposed and overthrown by the coming of Christ, saw the light come to the Gentiles and the saving light shine forth for the salvation of humankind, so that the deaf might receive the hearing of spiritual grace, the blind might open their eyes to God, the weak might recover strength through eternal health, the lame might run to the Church, and the mute might pray with clear voices and prayers; he saw idols abandoned and his own seats and temples deserted because of the great multitude of believers—and so he devised a new fraud, that under the very title of the Christian name he might deceive the unsuspecting? He has invented heresies and schisms by which he might subvert the faith, corrupt the truth, and tear apart unity. Those whom he cannot hold in the blindness of the old way, he encircles and deceives by the error of a new way. He snatches men from the Church itself; and while they appear to have drawn near to the light and escaped the darkness of the world, he pours fresh darkness into them unawares, so that, though they do not stand with the Gospel of Christ and with its observance and law, they call themselves Christians, and, walking in darkness, they think they possess the light—while the adversary flatters and deceives, transforming himself into an angel of light and his ministers into ministers of righteousness, as the Apostle says (2 Corinthians 11:14-15), declaring night to be day, destruction to be salvation, despair under the guise of hope, perfidy under the guise of faith, antichrist under the name of Christ; so that, while they utter plausible lies, they defeat the truth by subtlety. This happens, my dearest brothers, because we do not return to the origin of truth, nor seek the head, nor preserve the doctrine of the heavenly Master.
notes: Open enemies vs subtle schism/heresy.
latin: Cavenda sunt autem, fratres dilectissimi, non solum quae sunt aperta atque manifesta, sed et astutae fraudis subtilitate fallentia. Quid vero astutius, quidve subtilius, quam ut Christi adventu detectus ac prostratus inimicus, postquam lux Gentibus venit et sospitandis hominibus salutare lumen effulsit, ut surdi auditum gratiae spiritalis admitterent, aperirent ad Deum oculos suos caeci, infirmi aeterna sanitate revalescerent, claudi ad Ecclesiam currerent, muti claris vocibus et precibus orarent, videns ille idola derelicta et per nimium credentium populum sedes suas ac templa deserta, excogitaverit novam fraudem, ut sub ipso christiani nominis titulo fallat incautos? Haereses invenit et schismata, quibus subverteret fidem, veritatem corrumperet, scinderet unitatem. Quos detinere non potest in viae veteris caecitate, circumscribit et decipit novi itineris errore. Rapit de ipsa Ecclesia homines; et, dum sibi appropinquasse jam lumini atque evasisse saeculi noctem videntur, alias nescientibus tenebras rursus infundit, ut cum Evangelio Christi et cum observatione ejus et lege non stantes, Christianos se vocent, et ambulantes in tenebris habere se lumen existiment, blandiente adversario atque fallente, qui, secundum Apostoli vocem, transfigurat se velut angelum lucis, et ministros suos subornat velut ministros justitiae, asserentes noctem pro die, interitum pro salute, desperationem sub obtentu spei, perfidiam sub praetextu fidei, antichristum sub vocabulo Christi; ut, dum verisimilia mentiuntur, veritatem subtilitate frustrentur. Hoc eo fit, fratres dilectissimi, dum ad veritatis originem non reditur, nec caput quaeritur, nec magistri coelestis doctrina servatur.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 4
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: If any one consider and examine these things, there is no need for lengthened discussion and arguments. There is easy proof for faith in a short summary of the truth. The Lord speaks to Peter, saying, "I say unto you, that you are Peter; and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

And I will give unto you the keys of the kingdom of heaven; and whatsoever you shall bind on earth shall be bound also in heaven, and whatsoever you shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven." And again to the same He says, after His resurrection, "Feed my sheep." And although to all the apostles, after His resurrection, He gives an equal power, and says, "As the Father has sent me, even so send I you: Receive the Holy Ghost:

Whose soever sins you remit, they shall be remitted unto him; and whose soever sins you retain, they shall be retained; " John 20:21 yet, that He might set forth unity, He arranged by His authority the origin of that unity, as beginning from one. Assuredly the rest of the apostles were also the same as was Peter, endowed with a like partnership both of honour and power; but the beginning proceeds from unity.

Which one Church, also, the Holy Spirit in the Song of Songs designated in the person of our Lord, and says, "My dove, my spotless one, is but one. She is the only one of her mother, elect of her that bare her." Song of Songs 6:9 Does he who does not hold this unity of the Church think that he holds the faith?

Does he who strives against and resists the Church trust that he is in the Church, when moreover the blessed Apostle Paul teaches the same thing, and sets forth the sacrament of unity, saying, "There is one body and one spirit, one hope of your calling, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God? " Ephesians 4:4
notes: Peter/rock and one chair; equal share of honor among apostles yet unity from one.
latin: Loquitur Dominus ad Petrum: Ego tibi dico, inquit, quia tu es Petrus, et super hance petram aedificabo ecclesiam meam, et portae— inferorum non vincent eam. Dabo tibi claves regni caelorum; et quae ligaveris super terram, erunt ligata et in caelis, et quaecunque solveris super terram, erunt soluta et in caelis. Et iterum eidem post resurrectionem suam dicit: Pasce oves meas. Et quamvis apostolis omnibus post resurrectionem suam parem potestatem tribuat et dicat: Sicut misit me Pater, et ego mitto vos. Accipite Spiritum sanctum: si cuius remiseritis peccata, remittentur ill, si cuius tenueritis, tenebuntur; tamen ut unitatem manifestaret, unitatis eiusdem originem ab uno incipientem sua auctoritate disposuit. Hoc erant utique et caeteri apostoli, quod fuit Petrus, pari con- sortio praediti et honoris et potestatis, sed exordium ab unitate proficiscitur, ut ecclesia Christi una monstretur. Quam unam ecclesiam etiam in Cantico canticorum S

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 5
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: We must hold and defend this unity firmly, especially we bishops who preside over the Church, so that we may also prove that the episcopate itself is one and indivisible. No one is to deceive the brotherhood with a lie, and no one is to corrupt the truth of the faith with a faithless violation. The episcopate is one, and each bishop holds it in its entirety. The Church is also one, spreading wider into a multitude through the increase of her fruitfulness. Just as the sun has many rays but only one light, and a tree has many branches but one trunk rooted in a tenacious root, and many streams flow from a single spring — though the multitude may seem scattered by the generosity of its overflowing abundance, unity is still preserved at the source. If you tear a ray from the body of the sun, unity does not allow a division of light; if you break a branch from a tree, the broken branch cannot sprout; if you cut a stream from its source, the severed stream dries up. So too the Church of the Lord, filled with light, extends her rays throughout the whole world; yet the light is one, diffused everywhere, and the unity of the body is not divided. She spreads her branches over the whole earth with an abundance of fruitfulness, and her flowing streams expand widely with generous bounty; yet there is one head, one origin, and one mother of fruitfulness, rich in offspring. We are born from her womb, nourished by her milk, and given life by her Spirit.
notes: Episcopate one; many bishops share it; one church.
latin: Quam unitatem firmiter tenere et vindicare debemus, maxime episcopi, qui in Ecclesia praesidemus, ut episcopatum quoque ipsum unum atque indivisum probemus. Nemo fraternitatem mendacio fallat, nemo fidei veritatem perfida praevaricatione corrumpat. Episcopatus unus est, cujus a singulis in solidum pars tenetur. Ecclesia quoque una est, quae in multitudinem latius incremento foecunditatis extenditur. Quomodo solis multi radii, sed lumen unum; et rami arboris multi, sed robur unum tenaci radice fundatum; et cum de fonte uno rivi plurimi defluunt, numerositas licet diffusa videatur exundantis copiae largitate, unitas tamen servatur in origine. Avelle radium solis a corpore, divisionem lucis unitas non capit: ab arbore frange ramum, fractus germinare non poterit: a fronte praecide rivum, praecisus arescit. Sic et Ecclesia Domini luce perfusa per orbem totum radios suos porrigit; unum tamen lumen est, quod ubique diffunditur, nec unitas corporis separatur. Ramos suos in universam terram copia ubertatis extendit, profluentes largiter rivos latius expandit; unum tamen caput est et origo una, et una mater foecunditatis successibus copiosa. Illius foetu nascimur, illius lacte nutrimur, spiritu ejus animamur.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 7
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: This sacrament of unity, this bond of a concord inseparably cohering, is set forth where in the Gospel the coat of the Lord Jesus Christ is not at all divided nor cut, but is received as an entire garment, and is possessed as an uninjured and undivided robe by those who cast lots concerning Christ's garment, who should rather put on Christ.

Holy Scripture speaks, saying, "But of the coat, because it was not sewed, but woven from the top throughout, they said one to another, Let us not rend it, but cast lots whose it shall be." John 19:23-24 That coat bore with it an unity that came down from the top, that is, that came from heaven and the Father, which was not to be at all rent by the receiver and the possessor, but without separation we obtain a whole and substantial entireness.
He cannot possess the garment of Christ who parts and divides the Church of Christ.

On the other hand, again, when at Solomon's death his kingdom and people were divided, Abijah the prophet, meeting Jeroboam the king in the field, divided his garment into twelve sections, saying, "Take you ten pieces; for thus says the Lord, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give ten sceptres unto you; and two sceptres shall be unto him for my servant David's sake, and for Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen to place my name there." 1 Kings 11:31 As the twelve tribes of Israel were divided, the prophet Abijah rent his garment.

But because Christ's people cannot be rent, His robe, woven and united throughout, is not divided by those who possess it; undivided, united, connected, it shows the coherent concord of our people who put on Christ. By the sacrament and sign of His garment, He has declared the unity of the Church.
notes: Sacrament of unity; Lord’s coat without seam.
latin: Hoc unitatis sacramentum, hoc vinculum — concordiae inseparabiliter cohaerentis ostenditur, quando — in evangelio tunica Domini Iesu Christi non dividitur — omnino nec scinditur, sed sortientibus de veste Christi, — quis ipsam potius indueret, integra vestis accipitur et — incorrupta atque indivisa tunica possidetur. Loquitur CYPRIAN: DE UNITATE ECCLESIAE 19 5 6. The spouse of Christ cannot be defiled; het is uncorrupt and chaste. One home she knows; the sanctity of one chamber she guards with modesty and purity. It is she who keeps us for God, it is she who appoints unto the kingdom the sons she has borne. Whoever, separating himself from the Church, is joined to an adulteress, is cut off from the promises of the Church; nor will he who leaves the Church of Christ attain to Christ’s promises. He is an alien, a castaway, a foe. No longer can he have God for his father who has not the Church for his mother. If anyone was able to escape w

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 8
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: Who, then, is so wicked and faithless, who is so insane with the madness of discord, that either he should believe that the unity of God can be divided, or should dare to rend it — the garment of the Lord — the Church of Christ? He Himself in His Gospel warns us, and teaches, saying, "And there shall be one flock and one shepherd." John 10:16 And does any one believe that in one place there can be either many shepherds or many flocks?

The Apostle Paul, moreover, urging upon us this same unity, beseeches and exhorts, saving, "I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no schisms among you; but that you be joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment." 1 Corinthians 1:10 And again, he says, "Forbearing one another in love, endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace." Ephesians 4:3 Do you think that you can stand and live if you withdraw from the Church, building for yourself other homes and a different dwelling, when it is said to Rahab, in whom was prefigured the Church, "Your father, and your mother, and your brethren, and all the house of your father, you shall gather unto you into your house; and it shall come to pass, whosoever shall go abroad beyond the door of your house, his blood shall be upon his own head?

" Joshua 2:19 Also, the sacrament of the passover contains nothing else in the law of the Exodus than that the lamb which is slain in the figure of Christ should be eaten in one house. God speaks, saying, "In one house shall you eat it; you shall not send its flesh abroad from the house." Exodus 12:46 The flesh of Christ, and the holy of the Lord, cannot be sent abroad, nor is there any other home to believers but the one Church.

This home, this household of unanimity, the Holy Spirit designates and points out in the Psalms, saying, "God, who makes men to dwell with one mind in a house." Psalm 68:6 In the house of God, in the Church of Christ, men dwell with one mind, and continue in concord and simplicity:
notes: Can one who gathers elsewhere still be with Christ?

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 9
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: That is why the Holy Spirit also descended in the form of a dove — a simple, happy creature, neither bitter with gall nor savage with bites nor violent with claw-tearing. It loves human dwellings and knows the fellowship of a single household; when it breeds, the parents raise their young together; when it travels, the flock stays together in flight; it lives its whole life in common companionship, seals the concord of peace with a kiss of the mouth, and fulfills the law of unanimity in everything. This is the simplicity that must be recognized in the Church, and this is the charity that must be obtained, so that the love of doves may imitate brotherly love, and gentleness and mildness may equal the character of lambs and sheep. What place do the savagery of wolves, the rage of dogs, the lethal poison of serpents, and the bloody cruelty of beasts have in a Christian heart? It is a thing to rejoice when such people are separated from the Church, lest they devour the doves and the sheep of Christ with their savage and poisonous contagion. Bitterness cannot cohere and be joined with sweetness, darkness with light, rain with serenity, conflict with peace, sterility with fertility, dryness with springs, or tempest with tranquility. No one should think that good people can leave the Church: the wind does not carry away wheat, nor does a storm overturn a tree founded on a solid root; empty chaff is tossed about by a tempest, and weak trees are uprooted by the onslaught of a whirlwind. The apostle John condemns and strikes these people, saying, "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would certainly have remained with us" (1 John 2:19).
notes: Holy Spirit as dove; house one.
latin: Idcirco et in columba venit Spiritus sanctus: simplex animal et laetum, non felle amarum, non morsibus saevum, non unguium laceratione violentum, hospitia humana diligere, unius domus consortium nosse; cum generant, simul filios edere, cum commeant, volatibus invicem cohaerere, communi conversatione vitam suam degere, oris osculo concordiam pacis agnoscere, legem circa omnia unanimitatis implere. Haec est in Ecclesia noscenda simplicitas, haec charitas obtinenda, ut columbas dilectio fraternitatis imitetur, ut mansuetudo et lenitas agnis et ovibus aequetur. Quid facit in pectore christiano luporum feritas et canum rabies et venenum lethale serpentum et cruenta saevitia bestiarum? Gratulandum est cum tales de Ecclesia separantur, ne columbas, ne oves Christi saeva sua et venenata contagione praedentur. Cohaerere et conjungi non potest amaritudo cum dulcedine, caligo cum lumine, pluvia cum serenitate, pugna cum pace, cum foecunditate sterilitas, cum fontibus siccitas, cum tranquillitate tempestas. Nemo existimet bonos de Ecclesia posse discedere: triticum non rapit ventus, nec arborem solida radice fundatam procella subvertit; inanes paleae tempestate jactantur, invalidae arbores turbinis incursione evertuntur. Hos execratur et percutit Joannes apostolus dicens: Ex nobis exierunt, sed non fuerunt ex nobis: si enim fuissent ex nobis, mansissent utique nobiscum.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 10
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: From this, heresies have often arisen and still arise, while a perverse mind lacks peace and faithless discord fails to keep unity. Yet the Lord allows and endures these things, since the freedom of His own will remains, so that while He examines the discernment of truth in our hearts and minds, the unshaken faith of the tested may shine in clear light. Through the Apostle the Holy Spirit forewarns and says: "There must be heresies, so that those who are approved may be revealed among you" (1 Corinthians 11:19). Thus the faithful are proved, thus the faithless are exposed. Thus even now, before the day of judgment, the souls of the just and the unjust are already divided here, and the chaff is separated from the wheat. These are the ones who push themselves forward among the reckless without divine appointment, who set themselves up as prelates without any law of ordination, who take the title of bishop for themselves though no one has given them the episcopate. The Holy Spirit marks them in the Psalms as sitting in the chair of pestilence, as pests and plagues of the faith, deceiving with a serpent's mouth and crafting the corruption of truth, vomiting lethal poisons with pestilential tongues; their speech creeps like cancer, and their dealings pour mortal poison into the breasts and hearts of individuals.
notes: Heresies arise when unity is not kept.
latin: Hinc haereses et factae sunt frequenter et fiunt, dum perversa mens non habet pacem, dum perfidia discordans non tenet unitatem. Fieri vero haec Dominus permittit et patitur, manente propriae libertatis arbitrio, ut, dum corda nostra et mentes nostras veritatis discrimen examinat, probatorum fides integra manifesta luce clarescat. Per Apostolum praemonet Spiritus sanctus et dicit: Oportet haereses esse, ut probati manifesti sint in vobis. Sic probantur fideles, sic perfidi deteguntur. Sic et ante judicii diem hic quoque jam justorum atque injustorum animae dividuntur, et a frumento paleae separantur. Hi sunt qui se ultro apud temerarios convenas sine divina dispositione praeficiunt, qui, se praepositos sine ulla ordinationis lege constituunt, qui, nemine episcopatum dante, episcopi sibi nomen assumunt; quos designat in Psalmis Spiritus sanctus sedentes in pestilentiae cathedra, pestes et lues fidei, serpentis ore fallentes, et corrumpendae veritatis artifices, venena lethalia linguis pestiferis evomentes; quorum sermo ut cancer serpit, quorum tractatus pectoribus et cordibus singulorum mortale virus infundit.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 11
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: Against people of this kind the Lord cries; from these He restrains and recalls His erring people, saying, "Hearken not unto the words of the false prophets; for the visions of their hearts deceive them. They speak, but not out of the mouth of the Lord. They say to those who cast away the word of God, You shall have peace, and every one that walks after his own will. Every one who walks in the error of his heart, no evil shall come upon him.
I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.

If they had stood on my foundation (substantia, ὑποστα'σει), and had heard my words, and taught my people, I would have turned them from their evil thoughts." Jeremiah 23:16-21 Again, the Lord points out and designates these same, saying, "They have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, and have hewed them out broken cisterns which can hold no water." Jeremiah 2:13 Although there can be no other baptism but one, they think that they can baptize; although they forsake the fountain of life, they promise the grace of living and saving water.

Men are not washed among them, but rather are made foul; nor are sins purged away, but are even accumulated. Such a nativity does not generate sons to God, but to the devil. By a falsehood they are born, and they do not receive the promises of truth. Begotten of perfidy, they lose the grace of faith. They cannot attain to the reward of peace, since they have broken the Lord's peace with the madness of discord.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 12
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: Let no one deceive themselves with a vain interpretation of the Lord’s words: “Wherever two or three are gathered in my name, I am with them” (Matt. 18:20). Corrupters of the Gospel and false interpreters place the last things first and pass over what precedes, remembering one part while subtly suppressing another; just as they themselves are cut off from the Church, so they tear apart the meaning of a single passage. For when the Lord was urging His disciples toward unity and peace, He said: “I tell you, if two of you agree on earth about anything they ask, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven. For where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I among them,” showing that He grants more to the unity of those who pray than to their multitude. “If two of you agree on earth,” He said; He set unity first and sent peace ahead, so that He might teach us to come together faithfully and firmly. How, then, can a person come together with Him when they do not come together with the body of the Church itself and with the whole brotherhood? How can two or three be gathered in the name of Christ when it is clear that they are separated from Christ and from His Gospel? It was not we who separated from them, but they from us. And when heresies and schisms arose later, while they set up rival conventicles for themselves, they abandoned the head and source of truth. The Lord, however, speaks concerning His Church and addresses those who are in the Church, so that if they are of one mind—if even two or three are gathered in unity and pray—they may obtain from God’s majesty what they ask. “Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am with them,” He said—with the simple and the peaceful, with those who fear God and keep His commandments. He declared He would be with these two or three, just as He was with the three youths in the fiery furnace; because they remained simple and united among themselves, He revived their spirit with dew while flames surrounded them. So also He was present with the two apostles shut in prison; because they were simple and united, He Himself opened the prison doors and set them back in the public square so they could hand on to the crowd the word they had faithfully preached. Therefore, when He sets forth and says in His commandments, “Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am with them,” He does not separate people from the Church which He Himself instituted and built. Rather, rebuking discord among the faithless and commending peace to the faithful with His own voice, He shows that He is more truly with two or three who pray in unity than with many who dissent, and that the harmonious prayer of a few obtains more than the discordant prayer of many.
notes: Mt 18:20 misused by schismatics.
latin: Nec se quidam vana interpretatione decipiant quod dixerit Dominus: Ubicumque fuerint duo aut tres collecti in nomine meo, ego cum eis sum. Corruptores Evangelii atque interpretes falsi extrema ponunt et superiora praetereunt, partis memores, et partem subdole comprimentes; ut ipsi ab Ecclesia scissi sunt, ita capituli unius sententiam scindunt: Dominus enim, cum discipulis suis unanimitatem suaderet et pacem: Dico, inquit, vobis quoniam, si duobus ex vobis convenerit in terra, de omni re quacumque petieritis, continget vobis a Patre meo qui in coelis est. Ubicumque enim fuerint duo aut tres collecti in nomine meo, ego cum eis sum, ostendens non multitudini, sed unanimitati deprecantium plurimum tribui. Si duobus, inquit, ex vobis convenerit in terra; unanimitatem prius posuit, concordiam pacis ante praemisit, ut conveniat nobis fideliter et firmiter docuit. Quomodo autem potest ei cum aliquo convenire cui cum corpore ipsius Ecclesiae et cum universa fraternitate non convenit? quomodo possunt duo aut tres in nomine Christi colligi quos constat a Christo et ab ejus Evangelio separari? Non enim nos ab illis, sed illi a nobis recesserunt. Et cum haereses et schismata postmodum nata sint, dum conventicula sibi diversa constituunt, veritatis caput atque originem reliquerunt. Dominus autem de Ecclesia sua loquitur, et ad hos qui sunt in Ecclesia loquitur, ut si ipsi concordes fuerint, si, secundum quod mandavit et monuit, duo aut tres licet, collecti unanimiter oraverint, duo aut tres licet sint, impetrare possint de Dei majestate quod postulant. Ubicumque fuerint duo aut tres collecti in nomine meo, ego, inquit, cum eis sum, cum simplicibus scilicet atque pacatis, cum Deum timentibus et Dei praecepta servantibus. Cum his duobus vel tribus licet esse se dixit, quomodo et cum tribus pueris in camino ignis fuit, et quia in Deum simplices atque inter se unanimes permanebant, flammis ambientibus medios spiritu roris animavit. Quomodo Apostolis duobus in custodia clausis, quia simplices, quia unanimes erant, ipse adfuit, ipse, resolutis carceris claustris, ut verbum quod fideliter praedicabant multitudini traderent, ad forum rursus imposuit. Quando ergo in praeceptis suis ponit et dicit: Ubi fuerint duo aut tres collecti in nomine meo, ego cum eis sum, non homines ab Ecclesia dividit qui instituit et fecit Ecclesiam, sed exprobrans discordiam perfidis, et fidelibus pacem sua voce commendans, ostendit magis esse secum duobus aut tribus unanimiter orantibus quam cum dissidentibus plurimis, plusque impetrari posse paucorum concordi prece quam discordiosa oratione multorum.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 13
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: When He gave the law of prayer, He added these words: 'And when you stand praying, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your sins' (Mark 11:25). He calls back from the altar anyone who comes to the sacrifice with a quarrel, and He commands that person first to be reconciled with his brother; then, returning in peace, to offer his gift to God (Matthew 5:23-24). For God did not look with favor on Cain's gifts (Genesis 4:3-5); the one who did not have peace with his brother because of jealous discord could not have God as his peacemaker. What peace, then, do the enemies of brothers promise themselves? What sacrifices do they imagine they are offering as rival priests? Or do they suppose that Christ is with them when they gather, when they are gathering outside Christ's Church?
notes: Law of prayer and peace before sacrifice/altar.
latin: Ideo et cum orandi legem daret, addidit dicens: Et cum steteritis ad orationem, remittite si quid habetis adversus aliquem, ut et Pater vester qui in coelis est remittat vobis peccata. Et ad sacrificium cum dissensione venientem revocat ab altari, et jubet prius concordare cum fratre, tunc cum pace redeuntem Deo munus offerre, quia nec ad Cain munera respexit Deus: neque enim pacatum habere Deum poterat, qui cum fratre pacem per zeli discordiam non habebat. Quam sibi igitur pacem promittunt inimici fratrum, quae sacrificia celebrare se credunt aemuli sacerdotum? An secum esse Christum cum collecti fuerint opinantur, qui extra Christi Ecclesiam colliguntur?

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 14
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: Even if such people are killed confessing the name, that stain is not washed away by blood; the inexpiable and grave fault of discord is not purified by suffering. (1 Cor 13:2–3) No one who is not in the Church can be a martyr, and no one who abandons the Church, which is destined to reign, can arrive at the kingdom. Christ gave us peace, commanded us to be harmonious and of one mind, and ordered that the covenant of love and charity be kept incorrupt and inviolate. Anyone who did not hold fast to brotherly charity cannot present himself as a martyr. The apostle Paul teaches and testifies to this when he says: if I have faith so as to move mountains but do not have charity, I am nothing; and if I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I hand over my body to be burned, but do not have charity, I gain nothing. (1 Cor 13:2–3) Charity is magnanimous, charity is kind; charity does not envy, does not act shamefully, is not puffed up, is not provoked, does not count up wrongs; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. Charity never fails. Never, he says, does charity fail. For it will always remain in the kingdom; it will endure forever in the unbroken unity of brotherly concord. (1 Cor 13:4–8) Discord cannot enter the kingdom of heaven; the one who violates Christ's love with perfidious division cannot share in the rewards of Christ, who said, "This is my commandment, that you love one another, just as I have loved you." (John 13:34) Whoever lacks charity lacks God. The voice of the blessed apostle John declares: "God is love, and whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him." (1 John 4:16) Those who refused to live in harmony in the Church of God cannot remain with God. Even if they are delivered to flames and fire, or thrown to the beasts and lay down their lives, the result will not be the crown of faith but the punishment of faithlessness; not the glorious outcome of religious virtue but the destruction of despair. Such a person can be killed, but cannot be crowned. Thus someone professes to be a Christian just as the devil often lies, claiming to be Christ himself, despite the Lord's own warning: "Many will come in my name, saying, 'I am the Christ,' and they will deceive many." (Matt 24:5) Just as that one is not the Christ though he deceives in the name, so also the one who does not remain in the truth of his Gospel and faith cannot be recognized as a Christian.
notes: Martyrdom outside the church does not wash schism.
latin: Tales etiamsi occisi in confessione nominis fuerint, macula ista nec sanguine abluitur: inexpiabilis et gravis culpa discordiae nec passione purgatur. Esse martyr non potest qui in Ecclesia non est: ad regnum pervenire non poterit qui eam quae regnatura est derelinquit. Pacem nobis Christus dedit, concordes atque unanimes esse praecepit, dilectionis et charitatis foedera incorrupta atque inviolata servari mandavit. Exhibere se non potest martyrem qui fraternam non tenuit charitatem. Docet hoc et contestatur Paulus apostolus dicens: Et si habuero fidem ita ut montes transferam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil sum. Et si in cibos pauperum distribuero omnia mea, et si tradidero corpus meum ut ardeam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil proficio. Charitas magnanima est, charitas benigna est, charitas non aemulatur, non agit perperam, non inflatur, non irritatur, non cogitat malum, omnia diligit, omnia credit, omnia sperat, omnia sustinet. Charitas numquam excidit. Numquam, inquit, excidit charitas. Haec enim semper in regno erit, haec in aeternum fraternitatis sibi cohaerentis unitate durabit. Ad regnum coelorum non potest pervenire discordia; ad praemia Christi, qui dixit, Hoc est mandatum meum, ut diligatis invicem, quemadmodum dilexi vos, pertinere non poterit qui dilectionem Christi perfida dissensione violavit. Qui charitatem non habet, Deum non habet. Joannis beati apostoli vox est: Deus, inquit, dilectio est; et qui manet in dilectione, in Deo manet, et Deus in illo manet. Cum Deo manere non possunt qui esse in Ecclesia Dei unanimes noluerunt. Ardeant licet flammis et ignibus traditi vel objecti bestiis animas suas ponant, non erit illa fidei corona, sed poena perfidiae; nec religiosae virtutis exitus gloriosus, sed desperationis interitus. Occidi talis potest, coronari non potest. Sic se christianum esse profitetur quomodo et Christum diabolus saepe mentitur, ipso Domino praemonente et dicente: Multi venient in nomine meo dicentes: Ego sum Christus, et multos fallent. Sicut ille Christus non est, quamvis fallat in nomine, ita nec christianus videri potest qui non permanet in Evangelii ejus et fidei veritate.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 15
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: To prophesy, cast out demons, and perform great works on earth is certainly a sublime and admirable thing, yet no one attains the kingdom of heaven merely by being found in all these things unless they walk in the observance of a right and just path (Matt 7:21-23). The Lord warns and says: "Many will say to me on that day, 'Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, cast out demons in your name, and perform great works in your name?' Then I will tell them plainly, 'I never knew you; depart from me, you who practice lawlessness.'" Righteousness is necessary so that anyone may merit God as judge; we must obey His precepts and admonitions so that our merits may receive their reward. In His Gospel, the Lord directed the way of our hope and faith with a brief summary: "The Lord your God is one" (Deut 6:4), and "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength" (Deut 6:5). "This is the first commandment; and the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself" (Mark 12:29-31). On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets. He taught unity and love together through His teaching, embracing all the prophets and the Law within two commandments. But who preserves that unity, who guards or even considers that love, when, driven mad by the fury of discord, they tear apart the Church, destroy faith, disturb peace, dissipate charity, and profane the sacrament?
latin: Nam et prophetare et daemonia excludere et virtutes magnas in terris facere sublimis utique et admirabilis res est, non tamen regnum coeleste consequitur quisquis in his omnibus invenitur, nisi recti et justi itineris observatione gradiatur. Denuntiat Dominus et dicit: Multi mihi dicent in illo die: Domine, Domine, nonne in tuo nomine prophetavimus, et in tuo nomine daemonia exclusimus, et in nomine tuo virtutes magnas fecimus? Et tunc dicam illis: Numquam vos cognovi; recedite a me, qui operamini iniquitatem. Justitia opus est ut promereri quis possit Deum judicem: praeceptis ejus et monitis obtemperandum est, ut accipiant merita nostra mercedem. Dominus in Evangelio suo, cum spei et fidei nostrae viam compendio breviante dirigeret: Dominus Deus tuus, inquit, Deus unus est; et: Diliges Dominum Deum tuum de toto corde tuo, et de tota anima tua, et de tota virtute tua. Hoc est primum mandatum; et secundum simile huic: Diliges proximum tuum tamquam te. In his duobus praeceptis tota lex pendet et prophetae. Unitatem simul et dilectionem magisterio suo docuit, prophetas omnes et legem praeceptis duobus inclusit. Quam vero unitatem servat, quam dilectionem custodit aut cogitat, qui, discordiae furore vesanus, Ecclesiam scindit, fidem destruit, pacem turbat, charitatem dissipat, sacramentum profanat?

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 17
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: The excessive and abrupt perfidy of many must not move or disturb us; rather, with the truth of the matter already foretold, it should strengthen our faith. Because certain men have begun to be such as were predicted beforehand, the rest of the brothers must beware of such people, since these things were also foretold, with the Lord instructing and saying, "But you, beware; behold, I have foretold everything to you" (Mark 13:23). Brothers, I beg you, avoid such men and bar pernicious talk from your side and ears as if it were a contagion of death, just as it is written: "I have hedged my ears with thorns; I will not listen to a wicked tongue" (Sirach 28:28). And again: "Bad company corrupts good character" (1 Corinthians 15:33). The Lord teaches and admonishes us to withdraw from such people. He says, "They are blind guides of the blind" (Matthew 15:14), and, "If the blind lead the blind, both will fall into a pit" (Matthew 15:14). Anyone separated from the Church must be shunned and avoided. Such a person is perverse and sins, and stands self-condemned. Does he think he is with Christ who acts against Christ's priests and separates himself from the fellowship of Christ's clergy and people? He bears arms against the Church and rebels against God's ordinance. He is an enemy of the altar, a rebel against Christ's sacrifice, faithless in faith, sacrilegious in religion, a disobedient servant, an impious son, a hostile brother. Having despised and abandoned the bishops and God's priests, he dares to set up another altar, to offer another prayer with illicit voices, and to profane the truth of the Lord's sacrifice through false sacrifices. He does not realize that whoever resists God's ordination is punished by divine retribution because of the audacity of his temerity.
latin: Non tamen nos moveat aut turbet multorum nimia et abrupta perfidia, sed potius fidem nostram, praenuntiante rei veritate, corroboret. Ut quidam tales esse coeperunt, quia haec ante praedicta sunt, ita caeteri fratres ab ejusmodi caveant, quia et haec ante praedicta sunt, instruente Domino et dicente: Vos autem cavete, ecce praedixi vobis omnia. Vitate, quaeso vos, fratres, ejusmodi homines, et a latere atque auribus vestris perniciosa colloquia velut contagium mortis arcete, sicut scriptum est: Sepi aures tuas spinis, et noli audire linguam nequam. Et iterum: Corrumpunt ingenia bona confabulationes pessimae: Docet Dominus et admonet a talibus recedendum. Caeci sunt, inquit, duces caecorum. Caecus autem caecum ducens, simul in foveam cadunt. Aversandus est talis atque fugiendus quisquis fuerit ab Ecclesia separatus. Perversus est hujusmodi et peccat, et est a semetipso damnatus. An esse sibi cum Christo videtur qui adversus sacerdotes Christi facit, qui se a cleri ejus et plebis societate secernit? Arma ille contra Ecclesiam portat, contra Dei dispositionem repugnat. Hostis altaris, adversus sacrificium Christi rebellis, pro fide perfidus, pro religione sacrilegus, inobsequens servus, filius impius, frater inimicus, contemptis episcopis et Dei sacerdotibus derelictis, constituere audet aliud altare, precem alteram illicitis vocibus facere, Dominicae hostiae veritatem per falsa sacrificia profanare, nec scire quoniam qui contra ordinationem Dei nititur, ob temeritatis audaciam, divina animadversione punitur.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 18
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english:
Kore, Dathan, and Abiron tried to claim the right to sacrifice for themselves in defiance of Moses and the priest Aaron, and they immediately paid the penalty for their attempt (Numbers 16:1-35). The earth, its bonds broken, opened into a deep chasm, and the gash of the splitting ground swallowed them alive as they stood. God's indignation did not strike only the ringleaders; it also fell on the other two hundred fifty men who had shared their fury and joined them in the same act of rebellion. Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them in swift vengeance, warning and showing that whatever the wicked attempt in order to destroy God's ordination by human will is done against God (Numbers 16:1-35).

King Uzziah likewise took a censer and violently seized the sacrifice for himself contrary to God's law; when the priest Azariah resisted him, he refused to obey or yield. He was confounded by divine indignation and marked on his forehead with a disfiguring leprosy, branded on the very part of the body where those who have earned the Lord are marked, because he had offended the Lord (2 Chronicles 26:16-21). And the sons of Aaron, who put unauthorized fire on the altar, which the Lord had not commanded, were instantly struck down in the Lord's sight, avenged (Leviticus 10:1-2).
notes: Korah/Dathan/Abiram vs priestly order.
latin: Sic Chore et Dathan et Abiron, qui sibi contra Moysen et Aaron sacerdotem sacrificandi licentiam vindicare conati sunt, poenas pro suis statim conatibus pependerunt. Terra, compagibus ruptis, in profundum sinum patuit, stantes atque viventes recedentis soli hiatus absorbuit. Nec tantum eos qui auctores fuerant Dei indignantis ira percussit, sed et caeteros ducentos quinquaginta participes ejusdem furoris et comites, qui coagulati cum iisdem simul ad audaciam fuerant, exiens a Domino ignis properata ultione consumpsit, admonens scilicet et ostendens contra Deum fieri quidquid improbi fuerint ad destruendam ordinationem Dei humana voluntate conati. Sic et Ozias rex, cum thuribulum ferens, et contra legem Dei sacrificium sibi violenter assumens, resistente sibi Azaria sacerdote, obtemperare nollet et cedere, divina indignatione confusus et leprae varietate in fronte maculatus est, ea parte corporis notatus offenso Domino ubi signantur qui Dominum promerentur. Et filii Aaron, qui imposuerunt altari ignem alienum, quem non praeceperat Dominus, in conspectu statim Domini vindicatis extincti sunt.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 19
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: Those who despise God's tradition, chase after alien doctrines, and introduce human teachings as their authority are precisely the ones who imitate and follow such men. The Lord reproaches and rebukes them in His Gospel, saying, "You reject the command of God, so that you may establish your own tradition" (Mark 7:9). This crime is worse than the sin the lapsed appear to have committed; those, though established in penance for their crime, pray to God with full satisfaction. Here the Church is sought and entreated; there the Church is resisted. Here necessity may have been the cause; there the will is held fast in wickedness. The one who lapsed harmed only himself; the one who attempts heresy or schism deceives many by drawing them along with him. Here the loss is of a single soul; there the danger threatens many. The lapsed man certainly knows he has sinned, and he laments and mourns; the other swells with pride in his own breast, takes pleasure in his own offenses, separates children from their mother, lures sheep away from the shepherd, and disrupts God's sacraments. When the lapsed man sins once, that one sins daily. Finally, the lapsed man, if he later attains martyrdom, can receive the promises of the kingdom; but the other, if killed outside the Church, cannot attain the Church's rewards.
notes: Despising God’s tradition / appointing illicit bishops.
latin: Quos imitantur scilicet atque sectantur qui, Dei traditione contempta, alienas doctrinas appetunt et magisteria humanae institutionis inducunt; quos increpat Dominus et objurgat in Evangelio suo dicens: Rejicitis mandatum Dei, ut traditionem vestram statuatis. Pejus hoc crimen est quam quod admisisse lapsi videntur; qui tamen in poenitentia criminis constituti Deum plenis satisfactionibus deprecantur. Hic Ecclesia quaeritur et rogatur, illic Ecclesiae repugnatur. Hic potest necessitas fuisse, illic voluntas tenetur in scelere. Hic qui lapsus est sibi tantum nocuit, illic qui haeresim vel schisma facere conatus est multos secum trahendo decepit. Hic animae unius est damnum, illic periculum plurimorum. Certe peccasse se hic et intelligit, et lamentatur et plangit; ille tumens in pectore suo, et in ipsis sibi delictis placens, a matre filios segregat, oves a pastore sollicitat, Dei sacramenta disturbat: et cum lapsus semel peccaverit, ille quotidie peccat. Postremo lapsus, martyrium postmodum consecutus, potest regni promissa percipere; ille, si extra Ecclesiam fuerit occisus, ad Ecclesiae non potest praemia pervenire.

excerpts.citation: Cyprian — On the Unity of the Church 23
excerpts.author: Cyprian
excerpts.work: On the Unity of the Church
english: I want this, dearest brothers, and I both advise and urge it: if it is at all possible, may not a single brother perish, and may our mother, the Church, rejoice as she holds the whole consenting people in her bosom. Yet if certain leaders of schism and authors of dissension persist in blind, obstinate madness and sound counsel cannot bring them back to the way of salvation, the rest of you — whether taken in by simplicity, led astray by error, or tricked by some deceitful cunning — must free yourselves from the snares of fallacy, liberate your wandering steps from error, and recognize the straight path of the heavenly way.
