excerpts.author: Clement of Rome
english: The church of God that sojourns in Rome writes to the church of God that sojourns in Corinth — to those who are called and sanctified in God's will through our Lord Jesus Christ. May grace and peace be multiplied to you from Almighty God through Jesus Christ.

Because of the sudden and repeated calamities and misfortunes that have befallen us, we consider it time to turn to the matters you have asked about, beloved. These matters are foreign and alien to God's elect: a wicked and unholy rebellion that a few headstrong and arrogant persons have fanned into such madness that your honorable, renowned, and universally beloved name has been greatly blasphemed.

For who has visited you and not approved your blameless and firm faith? Who has not marveled at your prudent and gentle piety in Christ? Who has not proclaimed the magnificent character of your hospitality? Who has not pronounced a blessing on your complete and secure knowledge?

For you did everything without partiality and walked in God's lawful ways, submitting to your leaders and giving due honor to the elders among you. You allowed the young to think moderate and honorable thoughts. You commanded the women to carry out everything with a blameless, honorable, and pure conscience, loving their own husbands as is fitting. You taught those in the order of submission to manage the household honorably, with great prudence.
greek: Ἡ ἐκκλησία τοῦ θεοῦ ἡ παροικοῦσα Ῥώμην τῆ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ παροικούσῃ Κόρινθον, κλητοῖς ἡγιασμένοις ἐν θελήματι θεοῦ διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ παντοκράτορος θεοῦ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πληθυνθείη. Διὰ τὰς αἰφνιδίους καὶ ἐπαλλήλους γενομένας ἡμῖν συμφορὰς καὶ περιπτώσεις, βράδιον νομίζομεν ἐπιστροφὴν πεποιῆσθαι περὶ τῶν ἐπιζητουμένων παῤ ὑμῖν πραγμάτων, ἀγαπητοί, τῆς τε ἀλλοτρίας καὶ ξένης τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς τοῦ θεοῦ, μιαρᾶς καὶ ἀνοσίου στάσεως ἣν ὀλίγα πρόσωπα προπετῆ καὶ αὐθάδη ὑπάρχοντα εἰς τοσοῦτον ἀπονοίας ἐξέκαυσαν, ὥστε τὸ σεμνὸν καὶ περιβόητον καὶ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ἀξιαγάπητον ὄνομα ὑμῶν μεγάλως βλασφημηθῆναι. τίς γὰρ παρεπιδημήσας πρὸς ὑμᾶς τὴν πανάρετον καὶ βεβαίαν ὑμῶν πίστιν οὐκ ἐδοκίμασεν; τήν τε σώφρονα καὶ ἐπιεικῆ ἐν Χριστῷ εὐσέβειαν οὐκ ἐθαύμασεν; καὶ τὸ μεγαλοπρεπὲς τῆς φιλοξενίας ὑμῶν ἦθος οὐκ ἐκήρυξεν; καὶ τὴν τελείαν καὶ ἀσφαλῆ γνῶσιν οὐκ ἐμακάρισεν; ἀπροσωπολήμπτως γὰρ πάντα ἐποιεῖτε καὶ ἐν τοῖς νομίμοις τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπορεύεσθε, ὑποτασσόμενοι τοῖς ἡγουμένοις ὑμῶν, καὶ τιμὴν τὴν καθήκουσαν ἀπονέμοντες τοῖς παῤ ὑμῖν πρεσβυτέροις: νέοις τε μέτρια καὶ σεμνὰ νοεῖν ἐπετρέπετε: γυναιξίν τε ἐν ἀμώμῳ καὶ σεμνῇ καὶ ἁγνῇ συνειδήσει πάντα ἐπιτελεῖν παρηγγέλλετε, στεργούσας καθηκόντως τοὺς ἄνδρας ἑαυτῶν: ἔν τε τῷ κανόνι τῆς ὑποταγῆς ὑπαρχούσας τὰ κατὰ τὸν οἶκον σεμνῶς οἰκουργεῖν ἐδιδάσκετε, πάνυ σωφρονούσας.

excerpts.author: Clement of Rome
english: All of you kept a humble mind and refused to be arrogant, choosing to submit rather than to command, and you found more joy in giving than in receiving. You were content with the teachings of Christ and attended to His words carefully, treasuring them deep in your hearts, while His sufferings remained constantly before your eyes. Because of this, a deep and rich peace was given to everyone, an insatiable desire for doing good took hold, and a full outpouring of the Holy Spirit came upon all. Filled with holy purpose, you stretched out your hands to the Almighty God with eager readiness and reverent confidence, begging Him to show mercy if you had sinned unwillingly. Day and night you struggled for the whole brotherhood, praying that the number of His elect would be saved with mercy and a clear conscience. You were sincere, uncorrupted, and unforgetting of wrongs toward one another; every uprising and every division was detestable to you. You mourned over the transgressions of your neighbors and judged their failings as your own. You never regretted any good deed and stood ready for every good work. Adorned with all virtue and reverent conduct, you carried out everything in the fear of Him, for the Lord's commandments and righteous decrees were written on the very tablets of your hearts.
greek: Πάντες τε ἐταπεινοφρονεῖτε μηδὲν ἀλαζονευόμενοι, ὑποτασσόμενοι μᾶλλον ἦ ὑποτάσσοντες, ἥδιον διδόντες ἢ λαμβάνοντες. τοῖς ἐφοδίοις τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀρκούμενοι, καὶ προσέχοντες τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ ἐπιμελῶς ἐνεστερνισμένοι ἥτε τοῖς σπλάγχνοις, καὶ τὰ παθήματα αὐτοῦ ἦν πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν ὑμῶν. οὕτως εἰρήνη βαθεῖα καὶ λιπαρὰ ἐδέδοτο πᾶσιν καὶ ἀκόρεστος πόθος εἰς ἀγαθοποιΐαν, καὶ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου ἔκχυσις ἐπὶ πάντας ἐγίνετο: μεστοί τε ὁσίας βουλῆς, ἐν ἀγαθῇ προθυμίᾳ μετ’ εὐσεβοῦς πεποιθήσεως ἐξετείνετε τὰς χεῖρας ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν παντοκράτορα θεόν, ἱκετεύοντες αὐτὸν ἵλέως γενέσθαι, εἴ τι ἄκοντες ἡμάρτετε. ἀγὼν ἦν ὑμῖν ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὑπὲρ πάσης τῆς ἀδελφότητος, εἰς τὸ σώζεσθαι μετ’ ἐλέους καὶ συνειδήσεως τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ. εἰλικρινεῖς καὶ ἀκέραιοι ἦτε καὶ ἀμνησίκακοι εἰς ἀλλήλους. πᾶσα στάσις καὶ πᾶν σχίσμα βδελυκτὸν ἦν ὑμῖν. ἐπὶ τοῖς παραπτώμασιν τῶν πλησίον ἐπενθεῖτε: τὰ ὑστερήματα αὐτῶν ἴδια ἐκρίνετε. ἀμεταμέλητοι ἦτε ἐπὶ πάσῃ ἀγαθοποιΐᾳ, ἕτοιμοι εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθόν. τῇ παναρέτῳ καὶ σεβασμίῳ πολιτείᾳ κεκοσμημένοι πάντα ἐν τῷ φόβῳ αὐτοῦ ἐπετελεῖτε: τὰ προστάγματα καὶ τὰ δικαιώματα τοῦ κυρίου ἐπὶ τὰ πλάτη τῆς καρδίας ὑμῶν ἐγέγραπτο.

excerpts.author: Clement of Rome
english: Every glory and expansion were given to you, and what was written was fulfilled: He ate and drank, grew large, grew fat, and the beloved kicked. From this came zeal and envy, strife and faction, persecution and instability, war and captivity. Thus the dishonored rose up against the honored, the inglorious against the glorious, the foolish against the wise, the young against the elders. Because of this, righteousness and peace are far off, since each one abandons the fear of God and grows dim-sighted in faith, neither walking in the lawful requirements of His commands nor living as befits Christ, but each one walking according to the desires of his own evil heart, having taken up unjust and impious zeal, through which death also entered the world.
greek: Πᾶσα δόξα καὶ πλατυσμὸς ἐδόθη ὑμῖν, καὶ ἐπετελέσθη τὸ γεγραμμένον: Ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔπιεν, καὶ ἐπλατύνθη, καὶ ἐπαχύνθη, καὶ ἀπελάκτισεν ὁ ἠγαπημένος. ἐκ τούτου ζῆλος καὶ φθόνος, καὶ ἔρις, καὶ στάσις, διωγμὸς καὶ ἀκαταστασία, πόλεμος καὶ αἰχμαλωσία. οὕτως ἐπηγέρθησαν οἱ ἄτιμοι ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐντίμους, οἱ ἄδοξοι ἐπὶ τοὺς ἐνδόξους, οἱ ἄφρονες ἐπὶ τοὺς φρονίμους, οἱ νέοι ἐπὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους. διὰ τοῦτο πόρρω ἄπεστιν ἡ δικαιοσύνη καὶ εἰρήνη, ἐν τῷ ἀπολιπεῖν ἕκαστον τὸν φόβον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ πίστει αὐτοῦ ἀμβλυωπῆσαι, μηδὲ ἐν τοῖς νομίμοις τῶν προσταγμάτων αὐτοῦ πορεύεσθαι, μηδὲ πολιτεύεσθαι κατὰ τὸ καθῆκον τῷ Χριστῷ, ἀλλὰ ἕκαστον βαδίζειν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ τῆς πονηρᾶς, ζῆλον ἄδικον καὶ ἀσεβῆ ἀνειληφότας, δἰ οὖ καὶ θάνατος εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον.

excerpts.author: Clement of Rome
english: Each of us, brothers, must be pleasing to God in his own rank with a clear conscience, not overstepping the appointed rule of his ministry, and doing so with reverence. Sacrifices of intercession, prayers, or offerings for sin and transgression are not made just anywhere, brothers, but only in Jerusalem — and even there they are not offered in every place, but only before the temple at the altar, after the offering has been examined by the high priest and the ministers already mentioned. Therefore, anyone who acts contrary to God's will incurs the penalty of death. Notice, brothers: the more knowledge we have been deemed worthy of, the more danger we face.
greek: Ἕκαστος ἡμῶν, ἀδελφοί, ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι εὐαριστείτω τῷ θεῷ ἐν ἀγαθῇ συνειδήσει ὑπάρχων, μὴ παρεκβαίνων τὸν ὡρισμένον τῆς λειτουργίας αὐτοῦ κανόνα, ἐν σεμνότητι. οὐ πανταχοῦ, ἀδελφοί, προσφέρονται θυσίαι ἐνδελεχισμοῦ ἢ εὐχῶν ἢ περὶ ἁμαρτίας καὶ πλημμελείας, ἀλλ’ ἢ ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ μόνῃ: κἀκεῖ δὲ οὐκ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ προσφέρεται, ἀλλ’ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ναοῦ πρὸς τὸ θυσιαστήριον, μωμοσκοπηθὲν τὸ προσφερόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τῶν προειρημένων λειτουργῶν. οἱ οὖν παρὰ τὸ καθῆκον τῆς βουλήσεως αὐτοῦ ποιοῦντές τι θάνατον τὸ πρόστιμον ἔχουσιν. ὁρᾶτε, ἀδελφοί: ὅσῳ πλείονος κατηξιώθημεν γνώσεως, τοσούτῳ μᾶλλον ὑποκείμεθα κινδύνῳ.

excerpts.author: Clement of Rome
english: Take up the letter of the blessed apostle Paul and consider what he wrote to you at the very beginning of the gospel. He truly wrote to you under the Spirit's guidance about himself, Cephas, and Apollos, because even then you had formed factions. But that division brought you a lesser sin, since you were aligning yourselves with apostles who had been testified to and with a man approved by them. Now consider who has led you astray and diminished the noble character of your renowned brotherly love. It is shameful, beloved, utterly shameful, and unworthy of the conduct that belongs to life in Christ, that the most established and ancient church of the Corinthians should be in rebellion against its presbyters because of one or two persons. This report has reached not only us, but also those who differ from us, so that blasphemies are heaped on the Lord's name because of your folly, and you are bringing danger upon yourselves.
greek: Ἀναλάβετε τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου τοῦ ἀποστόλου. τί πρῶτον ὑμῖν ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἔγραψεν ; ἐπ’ ἀληθείας πνευματικῶς ἐπέστειλεν ὑμῖν περὶ ἑαυτοῦ τε καὶ Κηφᾶ τε καὶ Ἀπολλώ, διὰ τὸ καὶ τότε προσκλίσεις ὑμᾶς πεποιῆσθαι. ἀλλ’ ἡ πρόσκλισις ἐκείνη ἥττονα ἁμαρτίαν ὑμῖν προσήνεγκεν: προσεκλίθητε γὰρ ἀποστόλοις μεμαρτυρημένοις καὶ ἀνδρὶ δεδοκιμασμένῳ παῤ αὐτοῖς. νυνὶ δὲ κατανοήσατε, τίνες ὑμᾶς διέστρεψαν καὶ τὸ σεμνὸν τῆς περιβοήτου φιλαδελφίας ὑμῶν ἐμείωσαν. αἰσχρά, ἀγαπητοί, καὶ λίαν αἰσχρά, καὶ ἀνάξια τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ ἀγωγῆς ἀκούεσθαι, τὴν βεβαιοτάτην καὶ ἀρχαίαν Κορινθίων ἐκκλησίαν δἰ ἓν ἢ δύο πρόσωπα στασιάζειν πρὸς τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους: καὶ αὕτη ἡ ἀκοὴ οὐ μόνον εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐχώρησεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἑτεροκλινεῖς ὑπάρχοντας ἀφ̓ ἡμῶν, ὥστε καὶ βλασφημίας ἐπιφέρεσθαι τῷ ὀνόματι κυρίου διὰ τὴν ὑμετέραν ἀφροσύνην, ἑαυτοῖς δὲ κίνδυνον ἐπεξεργάζεσθαι.

excerpts.author: Clement of Rome
english: Let anyone who has love in Christ obey Christ's commands. Who can possibly explain the bond of God's love? Who is sufficient to describe the greatness of his beauty? The height to which love lifts us is unspeakable. Love binds us to God. Love covers a multitude of sins. Love endures everything and is patient in all things. There is nothing savage in love, nothing arrogant. Love creates no division; love does not rebel. Love does all things in harmony. In love, all God's elect were perfected, and without love, nothing is pleasing to God. In love, the Master welcomed us. Because of the love he had for us, Jesus Christ our Lord gave his blood for us according to God's will, and his flesh for our flesh and his soul for our souls.
greek: Ὁ ἔχων ἀγάπην ἐν Χριστῷ ποιησάτω τὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ παραγγέλματα. τὸν δεσμὸν τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ θεοῦ τίς δύναται ἐξηγήσασθαι; τὸ μεγαλεῖον τῆς καλλονῆς αὐτοῦ τίς ἀρκετὸς ἐξειπεῖν; τὸ ὕψος, εἰς ὃ ἀνάγει ἡ ἀγάπη, ἀνεκδιήγητόν ἐστιν. ἀγάπη κολλᾷ ἡμᾶς τῷ θεῷ, ἀγάπη καλύπτει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν, ἀγάπη πάντα ἀνέχεται, πάντα μακροθυμεῖ: οὐδὲν βάναυσον ἐν ἀγάπῃ, οὐδὲν ὑπερήφανον: ἀγάπη σχίσμα οὐκ ἔχει, ἀγάπη οὐ στασιάζει, ἀγάπη πάντα ποιεῖ ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ: ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ ἐτελειώθησαν πάντες οἱ ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ, δίχα ἀγάπης οὐδὲν εὐάρεστόν ἐστιν τῷ θεῷ. ἐν ἀγάπῃ προσελάβετο ἡμᾶς ὁ δεσπότης: διὰ τὴν ἀγάπην, ἣν ἔσχεν πρὸς ἡμᾶς, τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἔδωκεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν ἐν θελήματι θεοῦ, καὶ τὴν σάρκα ὑπὲρ τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν.

excerpts.author: Clement of Rome
english: Who among you is noble? Who is kind-hearted? Who is fully assured in love? Let that person speak up: 'If my presence has caused strife, quarreling, and division, I will step aside and leave. I will go wherever you wish, and I will do whatever the majority decides. Only let Christ's flock live at peace with the appointed presbyters.' The one who does this will win great glory for himself in Christ, and every place will welcome him, for the earth and all it contains belong to the Lord (Psalm 24:1). This is what those who live as citizens of God's unregretted citizenship have done and will continue to do.
greek: Τίς οὖν ἐν ὑμῖν γενναῖος, τίς εὔσπλαγχνος, τίς πεπληροφορημένος ἀγάπης; εἰπάτω: Εἰ δἰ ἐμὲ στάσις καὶ ἔρις καὶ σχίσματα, ἐκχωρῶ, ἄπειμι, οὗ ἐὰν βούλησθε, καὶ ποιῶ τὰ προστασσόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ πλήθους: μόνον τὸ ποίμνιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰρηνευέτω μετὰ τῶν καθεσταμένων πρεσβυτέρων. τοῦτο ὁ ποιήσας ἑαυτῷ μέγα κλέος ἐν Χριστῷ περιποιήσεται, καὶ πᾶς τόπος δέξεται αὐτόν, τοῦ γὰρ κυρίου ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. ταῦτα οἱ πολιτευόμενοι τὴν ἀμεταμέλητον πολιτείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐποίησαν καὶ ποιήσουσιν.

excerpts.author: Clement of Rome
english: If some people disobey what he said through us, they need to realize that they will bind themselves to a serious sin and danger. We, however, will be innocent of this sin, and we will offer earnest prayer and petition so that the Creator of all things may keep the complete number of his elect throughout the world unbroken through his beloved child, Jesus Christ. Through Christ he called us out of darkness into light and out of ignorance into the knowledge of the glory of his name. We put our hope in the name of the Originator of all creation, since you have opened the eyes of our hearts to know you, the only Most High in the highest heavens, holy among the holy, the one who rests in holiness. You humble the pride of the arrogant, dissolve the schemes of nations, lift up the lowly and bring down the lofty, make rich and make poor, kill and make alive. You alone are the discerner of spirits and the God of all flesh. You look into the abysses, oversee human deeds, help those in danger, save the desperate, and are the creator and overseer of every spirit. You multiply nations on the earth and choose from all peoples those who love you through Jesus Christ, your beloved child, through whom you taught us, sanctified us, and honored us. Therefore we ask you, Master, to become our helper and supporter. Save those of us in distress, have mercy on the lowly, raise up the fallen, reveal yourself to those in need, heal the weak, and bring back the wandering among your people. Feed the hungry, ransom our captives, strengthen the feeble, encourage the fainthearted, and let all nations know you. For you alone are God, Jesus Christ is your child, and we are your people, the sheep of your pasture.
greek: Ἐὰν δέ τινες ἀπειθήσωσιν τοῖς ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δἰ ἡμῶν εἰρημένοις, γινωσκέτωσαν ὅτι παραπτώσει καὶ κινδύνῳ οὐ μικρῷ ἑαυτοὺς ἐνδήσουσιν. ἡμεῖς δὲ ἀθῷοι ἐσόμεθα ἀπὸ ταύτης τῆς ἁμαρτίας καὶ αἰτησόμεθα ἐκτενῆ τὴν δέησιν καὶ ἱκεσίαν ποιούμενοι, ὅπως τὸν ἀριθμὸν τὸν κατηριθμημένον τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ διαφυλάξῃ ἄθραυστον ὁ δημιουργὸς τῶν ἁπάντων διὰ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου παιδὸς αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, δἰ οὗ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς, ἀπὸ ἀγνωσίας εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν δόξης ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ, ... ἐλπίζειν ἐπὶ τὸ ἀρχεγόνον πάσης κτίσεως ὄνομά σου, ἀνοίξας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς τῆς καρδίας ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ γινώσκειν σε τὸν μόνον ὕψιστον ἐν ὑψίστοις, ἅγιον ἐν ἀγίοις ἀναπαυόμενον. τὸν ταπεινοῦντα ὕβριν ὑπερηφάνων, τὸν διαλύοντα λογισμοὺς ἐθνῶν, τὸν ποιοῦντα ταπεινοὺς εἰς ὕψος καὶ τοὺς ὑψηλοὺς ταπεινοῦντα, τὸν πλουτίζοντα καὶ πτωχίζοντα, τὸν ἀποκτείνοντα καὶ ζῆν ποιοῦντα, μόνον εὑρέτην πνευμάτων καὶ θεὸν πάσης σαρκός: τὸν ἐπιβλέποντα ἐν τοῖς ἀβύσσοις, τὸν ἐπόπτην ἀνθρωπίνων ἔργων, τὸν τῶν κινδυνευόντων βοηθόν, τὸν τῶν ἀπηλπισμένων σωτῆρα, τὸν παντὸς πνεύματος κτίστην καὶ ἐπίσκοπον: τὸν πληθύνοντα ἔθνη ἐπὶ γῆς καὶ ἐκ πάντων ἐκλεξάμενον τοὺς ἀγαπῶντάς σε διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ ἠγαπημένου παιδός σου, δἰ οὗ ἡμᾶς ἐπαίδευσας, ἡγίασας, ἐτίμησας: ἀξιοῦμέν σε, δέσποτα, βοηθὸν γενέσθαι καὶ ἀντιλήπτορα ἡμῶν. τοὺς ἐν θλίψει ἡμῶν σῶσον, τοὺς ταπεινοὺς ἐλέησον, τοὺς πεπτωκότας ἔγειρον, τοῖς δεομένοις ἐπιφάνηθι, τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς ἴασαι, τοὺς πλανωμένους τοῦ λαοῦ σου ἐπίστρεψον: χόρτασον τοὺς πεινῶντας, λύτρωσαι τοὺς δεσμίους ἡμῶν, ἐξανάστησον τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας, παρακάλεσον τοὺς ὀλιγοψυχοῦντας: γνώτωσάν σε ἅπαντα τὰ ἔθνη. ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ θεὸς μόνος καὶ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ παῖς σου καὶ ἡμεῖς λαός σου καὶ πρόβατα τῆς νομῆς σου.

excerpts.author: Cyprian
english: It is no wonder that they now reject our plans or the Lord's commandments, since they have denied the Lord. They crave fees, offerings, and profits, wallowing in them with the same insatiable greed as before. Even now they pant after dinners and feasts; they used to belch out the gluttony of those banquets in crude daily fashion, and now they prove most clearly that they served not religion before, but rather their belly and their gain with profane desire. We perceive and believe that a censure has come from God's scrutiny, lest they persist in standing at the altar and further handling the shame of incest, the faith of the perfidious, the religion of the profane, divine things as earthly, and holy things as sacrilegious. So that such people may not return again to the impious desecrations and contaminations of the brothers at the altar, we must stand guard with all our strength and strive with all our vigor to repel them, as far as we can, from the audacity of their own crime, lest they attempt to act as priests—men who, having been cast down to the very brink of death, have fallen beyond the fallen laity under the weight of a greater ruin.
notes: Mixed cup / eucharistic practice.
latin: Nec mirum si consilia nostra aut Domini praecepta nunc abnuunt qui Dominnm negaverunt: stipes et oblationes et lucra desiderant, quibus prius insatiabiles incubabant; et coenis atque epulis etiam nunc inhiant, quarum crapulam superstite nuper in dies cruditate ructabant, nunc manifestissime comprobantes nec ante se religioni, sed ventri potius et quaestui profana cupiditate servisse. Unde et ipsam venisse perspicimus et credimus de Dei exploratione censuram, ne apud altare consistere et contrectare ulterius perseverarent pudorem incesti, fidem perfidi, religionem profani, divina terreni, sancta sacrilegi. Quod ne tales ad altaris impiamenta et contagia fratrum denuo redeant, omnibus viribus excubandum est, et omni vigore nitendum ut quantum possumus ab hac eos sui sceleris audacia retundamus, ne adhuc agere pro sacerdote conentur qui ad mortis extrema dejecti, ultra lapsos laicos ruinae majoris pondere proruerunt.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: We have come to know the plan of our salvation through those who brought the Gospel to us. They first proclaimed it by word, then, by God's will, handed it down to us in the Scriptures, which were to become the foundation and pillar of our faith. It is not right to claim that they preached before they possessed full knowledge, as some presumptuously assert, boasting that they are correctors of the Apostles. For after our Lord rose from the dead, and they were clothed with power from on high when the Holy Spirit came upon them, they were filled with all things and attained perfect knowledge. They went out to the ends of the earth, preaching the good things that come to us from God and proclaiming heavenly peace to all people, each of them bearing the Gospel of God. Thus Matthew produced a written Gospel in the Hebrews' own language, while Peter and Paul were evangelizing in Rome and laying the foundations of the Church. After their departure, Mark, the disciple and interpreter of Peter, handed down to us in writing what had been announced by Peter. Luke, a follower of Paul, set down in a book the Gospel that Paul preached. Later, John, the disciple of the Lord who had leaned on His breast, published his Gospel while living at Ephesus in Asia. All of them proclaimed to us one God, the Maker of heaven and earth, announced by the Law and the Prophets, and one Christ, the Son of God. If anyone does not assent to them, he despises the Lord's companions, he despises Christ the Lord, he despises the Father, and he condemns himself by resisting and opposing his own salvation. This is what all heretics do.
notes: Apostles preached and deposited the gospel in the church.
latin: 1. Now enim per alios dispositionem salutis nostree cognovimus, quam per eos per quos Evangelium pervenit ad nos: quod quidem tune preeconayerunt, postea vero per Dei voluntatem in Seripturis nobis tradiderunt, fundamentum et columnam fidei nostree futurum. Nec enim fas est dicere, quoniam ante preedicaverunt quam perfectam haberent agnitionem; sicut quidam audent dicere, gloriantes emendatores se esse Apostolorum. Postea enim quam surrexit Dominus noster a mortuis, et induti sunt supervenientis Spiritus sancti virtutem ex alto, de omnibus adimpleti sunt, et habuerunt perfectam agnitionem; exierunt in fines terree, ea quee a Deo nobis bona sunt evangelizantes, et ccelestem pacem hominibus annuntiantes, qui quidem et omnes pariter et singuli eorum habentes Evangelium Dei*. Ita Mattheus in Hebreis ipsorum lingua scripturam y. edidit Evangelii, cum Petrus et Paulus Rome evangelizarent, et ecxdyoiav. Mera de trav fundarent Ecclesiam. Post vero horum excessum, Marcus discipulus et interpres Petri, et ipse quee a Petro annuntiata erant, per ———— seripta nobis tradidit. Et Lucas autem sectator Pauli, quod ab illo preedicabatur Evangelium, in libro condidit. Postea et Johannes discipulus Domini, qui et supra pectus ejus recumbebat, et ipse edidit Evangelium, Ephesi Asie commorans. Et omnes isti unum Deum factorem cceli et terre a lege et prophetis annuntiatum, et unum Christum filium Dei tradiderunt nobis: quibus si quis non assentit, spernit quidem participes Domini, spernit autem et ipsum Christum Dominum, spernit vero et Patrem, et est a semetipso damnatus, resistens et repugnans saluti suze: quod faciunt omnes heeretici.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: When they are refuted from the Scriptures, they turn around and accuse the Scriptures themselves, as if the Scriptures were not rightly constituted, lacked authority, and contradicted themselves because they were expressed in various ways. They claim that truth cannot be discovered from the Scriptures by those who do not know the tradition. After all, the tradition was handed down not in writing, but by living voice. That is why Paul said, "We speak wisdom among the mature, yet a wisdom not of this world" (1 Corinthians 2:6-7). Each of these heretics then claims that this wisdom is exactly what he has discovered on his own — an obvious fiction — so that truth may appear worthy on his own terms: at one time in Valentinus, at another in Marcion, then in Cerinthus, later in Basilides, and even in the one who argues against the rest, though he could speak nothing that saves. Every single one of them is thoroughly perverted, yet he preaches without shame, making himself the standard of truth.

But when we appeal to the tradition that comes from the Apostles — the tradition preserved in the Churches through the succession of Presbyters — they reject it. They boast that they are wiser not only than the Presbyters but even than the Apostles, because they have found the pure truth. They allege that the Apostles mixed legalistic elements into the Savior's words, and not only the Apostles but the Lord Himself: sometimes speaking from the Demiurge, sometimes from the Middle, sometimes from the Highest. They themselves, they claim, know the hidden mystery without doubt, without stain, purely. But this is nothing less than blaspheming their own Maker with utter insolence. Consequently, they agree with neither the Scriptures nor the tradition. Our struggle, dear friend, is against men who slip away on every side like slippery serpents. Therefore we must resist them on every side, so that by refuting them we may, if possible, bring some of them to the conversion of truth. For although it is not easy for a soul seized by error to recover, it is not entirely impossible to escape error when the truth is set before it.
notes: Heretics accuse Scriptures and claim secret tradition.
latin: 1. Cvum enim ex Seripturis arguuntur, in accusationem con-vertuntur ipsarum Seripturarum, quasi non recte habeant, neque sint ex auctoritate, et quia varie sint dictez, et quia non possit ex his inveniri veritas ab his qui nesciant traditionem. Non enim per literas traditam illam, sed per vivam vocem: ob quam causam et Paulum dixisse: Sapientiam autem loquimur inter perfectos: sapientiam autem non mundi hujus. Et hane sapientiam unusquisque eorum esse dicit, quam a semetipso adinvenit, fictionem videlicet, ut digne secundum eos sit veritas, aliquando quidem in Valentino, aliquando autem in Marcione, aliquando in Cerintho, postea deinde in Basilide, fuit aut et in illo qui contra disputat, qui nihil salutare loqui potuit. Unusquisque enim ipsorum omnimodo perversus, semetipsum regulam veritatis depravans preedicare non confunditur, ' 2. Cum autem ad eam iterum traditionem, que est ab Apostolis, quee per successiones Presbyterorum in Ecclesiis. custoditur, provocamus eos, adversantur traditioni, dicentes se non solum Presbyteris, sed etiam A postolis exsistentes sapientiores, sinceram invenisse veritatem. Apostolos enim admiscuisse ea que sunt legalia Salvatoris verbis: et non solum Apostolos, sed etiam ipsum Dominum, modo quidem a Demiurgo, modo autem a medietate, interdum autem a summitate fecisse sermones : se vero indubitate, et intaminate, et sincere absconditum scire mysterium: quod quidem impudentissime est blasphemare suum factorem. Eyenit itaque, neque Scripturis jam, neque traditioni consentire eos. Adversus tales certamen nobis est, o dilectissime, more serpentum lubrici [7. lubrice] undique effugere conantes. Quapropter undique resistendum est illis, si quos ex his retusione confundentes, ad conversionem veritatis adducere possimus. Etenim si non facile est ab errore apprehensam resipiscere animam, sed non omnimodo impossibile est errorem effugere apposita veritate.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: 1. It is within the power of all, therefore, in every Church, who may wish to see the truth, to contemplate clearly the tradition of the apostles manifested throughout the whole world; and we are in a position to reckon up those who were by the apostles instituted bishops in the Churches, and [to demonstrate] the succession of these men to our own times; those who neither taught nor knew of anything like what these [heretics] rave about.

For if the apostles had known hidden mysteries, which they were in the habit of imparting to the perfect apart and privily from the rest, they would have delivered them especially to those to whom they were also committing the Churches themselves.

For they were desirous that these men should be very perfect and blameless in all things, whom also they were leaving behind as their successors, delivering up their own place of government to these men; which men, if they discharged their functions honestly, would be a great boon [to the Church], but if they should fall away, the direst calamity.
notes: Apostolic tradition visible in every church via succession.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: They insisted that the men they were leaving behind as successors be thoroughly blameless and irreproachable in every respect, so that great benefit would come to those who would act in their place of teaching, while the greatest calamity would befall those who fell away. But because it would take far too long to list the successions of every church in a work of this scope, we will set forth the tradition that comes from the Apostles and the faith proclaimed to humanity, which has reached us through the succession of bishops from the most glorious two Apostles, Peter and Paul, who founded and established the church at Rome. By doing so we confound all those who, in any manner — whether through self-pleasing evil, empty glory, blindness, or bad judgment — gather in any way other than what is fitting. For every church must convene to this church on account of its more powerful principality; that is, the faithful from everywhere must come together here, because in this church the tradition that comes from the Apostles has always been preserved by those who come from everywhere.
notes: Tedious to list all successions; Rome as example confounds heretics.
latin: Valde enim fectos et irreprehensibiles in omnibus eos volebant esse, quos et successores relinquebant, suum ipsorum locum magisterii tradenemendate agentibus fieret magna utilitas, lapsis autem summa calamitas, Sed quoniam valde longum est, in hoe tali volumine omnium ecclesiarum enumerare successiones, maximz, et antiquissimz, et omnibus cognitz, a gloriosissimis duobus Apostolis ? Petro et Paulo Rome fundatz et constitute ecclesiz, eam quam habet ab Apostolis traditionem, et annuntiatam hominibus fidem, per successiones Episcoporum pervenientem .usque ad nos indicantes, confundimus omnes eos, qui quoquo modo vel per sibiplacentiam malam, vel vanam gloriam, vel per cecitatem et malam sententiam, preeterquam oportet colligunt. Ad hane enim ecclesiam propter potentiorem principalitatem necesse est omnem Sconvenire Ecclesiam, hoc est, eos qui sunt undique fideles, in qua semper ab his, qui sunt undique, conservata est ea que est ab Apostolis traditio.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: Therefore the blessed Apostles, having founded and instructed the Church, handed over the episcopate of the Church to Linus. Paul mentions this Linus in his letters to Timothy (1 Timothy). Anacletus succeeded him, and after him, in the third place from the Apostles, Clement obtained the episcopate. Clement had seen the Apostles themselves and conversed with them; he still had the Apostles' preaching and tradition before his eyes, for many who had been taught by the Apostles were still surviving at that time. Under his leadership, therefore, when a significant dissension had arisen among the brothers at Corinth, the Church at Rome wrote a most powerful letter to the Corinthians. It summoned them to peace, restored their faith, and announced the tradition Clement had recently received from the Apostles. That tradition proclaims one God, almighty, the maker of heaven and earth, the shaper of man, who brought the flood, who called Abraham, who led the people out of the land of Egypt, who spoke with Moses, who established the law, who sent the prophets, and who prepared fire for the devil and his angels. This Father of our Lord Jesus Christ is proclaimed by the churches from Scripture itself; those who wish to learn can know it and understand the apostolic tradition of the Church. For this letter is older than those who now falsely teach and invent another God above the Demiurge and Maker of all these things. After Clement, Evaristus succeeded; after Evaristus, Alexander; and next, sixth from the Apostles, Sixtus was appointed. From him came Telesphorus, who also underwent a most glorious martyrdom; then Hyginus, then Pius, after whom came Anicetus. When Soter succeeded Anicetus, Eleutherius now holds the episcopate from the Apostles in the twelfth place. This order and succession demonstrate the tradition that comes from the Apostles in the Church and the proclamation of the truth. It is a most complete demonstration that has come down to us: the same life-giving faith which was in the Church from the Apostles until now has been preserved and handed down in truth.
notes: Roman episcopal succession from Peter and Paul through Linus…
latin: Fundantes igitur et instruentes beati Apostoli Ecclesiam, Lino episcopatum administrande Ecclesiz tradiderunt. Hujus Lini Paulus in his que sunt ad Timotheum epistolis meminit. Succedit autem ei Anacletus: post eum tertio loco ab Apostolis episcopatum sortitur Clemens, qui et vidit ipsos Apostolos, et contulit cum eis, et cum adhuc insonantem preedicationem A postolorum et traditionem ante oculos haberet; non solus; adhuc enim multi supererant tune ab Apostolis docti.. Sub hoe igitur mente, dissensione non modica inter eos qui Corinthi essent fratres facta, scripsit quae est Romze Ecélesia potentissimas literas Corinthiis, ad pacem eos congregans, et reparans fidem eorum, et annuntians quam in recenti ab Apostolis acceperat traditionem, annuntiantem unum Deum omnipotentem, factorem cceli et terre, plasmatorem hominis, qui induxerit cataclysmum, et advocaverit Abraham, qui eduxerit populum de terra A®gypti, qui collocutus sit Moysi, qui legem disposuerit, et prophetas miserit, qui ignem preeparaverit diabolo et angelis ejus. Hune Patrem Domini nostri Jesu Christi ab ecclesiis annuntiari, ex ipsa scriptura, qui velint discere possunt, et apostolicam Ecclesize traditionem intelligere, cum sit vetustior epistola his qui nune falso docent, et alterum Deum super Demiurgum et factorem horum omnium que sunt commentiuntur, 8. Huie autem Clementi succedit Euaristus, et Euaristo Alexander, ac deinceps sextus ab Apostolis constitutus est Sixtus, et ab hoc Telesphorus, qui etiam gloriosissime martyrium fecit: ac deinceps Hyginus, post Pius, post quem Anicetus. Cum autem successisset Aniceto Soter, nunc duodecimo loco Episcopatum ab Apostolis habet Eleutherius. Hac ordinatione et successione ea quee est ab Apostolis in Ecclesia traditio et veritatis praeconatio Et est plenissima hee ostensio, unam et pervenit usque ad nos. eandem vivificatricem fidem esse, quae in Ecclesia ab Apostolis usque nunc sit conservata, et tradita in veritate> 4.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: But Polycarp also was not only instructed by apostles, and conversed with many who had seen Christ, but was also, by apostles in Asia, appointed bishop of the Church in Smyrna, whom I also saw in my early youth, for he tarried [on earth] a very long time, and, when a very old man, gloriously and most nobly suffering martyrdom, departed this life, having always taught the things which he had learned from the apostles, and which the Church has handed down, and which alone are true.

To these things all the Asiatic Churches testify, as do also those men who have succeeded Polycarp down to the present time — a man who was of much greater weight, and a more steadfast witness of truth, than Valentinus, and Marcion, and the rest of the heretics.

He it was who, coming to Rome in the time of Anicetus caused many to turn away from the aforesaid heretics to the Church of God, proclaiming that he had received this one and sole truth from the apostles — that, namely, which is handed down by the Church.

There are also those who heard from him that John, the disciple of the Lord, going to bathe at Ephesus, and perceiving Cerinthus within, rushed out of the bath-house without bathing, exclaiming, Let us fly, lest even the bath-house fall down, because Cerinthus, the enemy of the truth, is within. And Polycarp himself replied to Marcion, who met him on one occasion, and said, Do you know me? I do know you, the first-born of Satan.

Such was the horror which the apostles and their disciples had against holding even verbal communication with any corrupters of the truth; as Paul also says, A man that is an heretic, after the first and second admonition, reject; knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sins, being condemned of himself.

Titus 3:10 There is also a very powerful Epistle of Polycarp written to the Philippians, from which those who choose to do so, and are anxious about their salvation, can learn the character of his faith, and the preaching of the truth. Then, again, the Church in Ephesus, founded by Paul, and having John remaining among them permanently until the times of Trajan, is a true witness of the tradition of the apostles.
notes: Polycarp and Asian churches against Valentinus/Marcion.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: 1. Since therefore we have such proofs, it is not necessary to seek the truth among others which it is easy to obtain from the Church; since the apostles, like a rich man [depositing his money] in a bank, lodged in her hands most copiously all things pertaining to the truth: so that every man, whosoever will, can draw from her the water of life. Revelation 22:17 For she is the entrance to life; all others are thieves and robbers.

On this account are we bound to avoid them, but to make choice of the thing pertaining to the Church with the utmost diligence, and to lay hold of the tradition of the truth. For how stands the case? Suppose there arise a dispute relative to some important question among us, should we not have recourse to the most ancient Churches with which the apostles held constant intercourse, and learn from them what is certain and clear in regard to the present question?

For how should it be if the apostles themselves had not left us writings? Would it not be necessary, [in that case,] to follow the course of the tradition which they handed down to those to whom they did commit the Churches? 2.

To which course many nations of those barbarians who believe in Christ do assent, having salvation written in their hearts by the Spirit, without paper or ink, and, carefully preserving the ancient tradition, believing in one God, the Creator of heaven and earth, and all things therein, by means of Christ Jesus, the Son of God; who, because of His surpassing love towards His creation, condescended to be born of the virgin, He Himself uniting man through Himself to God, and having suffered under Pontius Pilate, and rising again, and having been received up in splendour, shall come in glory, the Saviour of those who are saved, and the Judge of those who are judged, and sending into eternal fire those who transform the truth, and despise His Father and His advent.

Those who, in the absence of written documents, have believed this faith, are barbarians, so far as regards our language; but as regards doctrine, manner, and tenor of life, they are, because of faith, very wise indeed; and they do please God, ordering their conversation in all righteousness, chastity, and wisdom.

If any one were to preach to these men the inventions of the heretics, speaking to them in their own language, they would at once stop their ears, and flee as far off as possible, not enduring even to listen to the blasphemous address.

Thus, by means of that ancient tradition of the apostles, they do not suffer their mind to conceive anything of the [doctrines suggested by the] portentous language of these teachers, among whom neither Church nor doctrine has ever been established.
notes: Even without writings, barbarian churches keep ancient tradition.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: Therefore, if anyone reads the Scriptures with intent, he will find in them a message concerning Christ and a prefiguring of the new calling. For this is the treasure hidden in the field—that is, in this world, for the field is the world—and the treasure hidden in the Scriptures is Christ, since he was signified through types and parables. How could this reality which belongs to his humanity be understood before the consummation of those things that have been consummated arrived, that is, the advent of Christ? And because of this it was said to the prophet Daniel: "Seal the words, and seal the book until the time of consummation, until many learn and knowledge is fulfilled" (Daniel). For when the dispersion is perfected, all will know these things. Jeremiah also says: "In the last days they will understand these things" (Jeremiah). For every prophecy, before it has its effect, is signs and ambiguities to men. But when the time comes and what has been prophesied happens, then the prophecies have a clear and certain exposition. And because of this, to the Jews, when the Law is read in this present time, it is like fables; for they do not have the exposition of all things pertaining to the advent of the Son of God, who is according to humanity. But to Christians, when it is read, it is a treasure hidden in the field, revealed by the cross of Christ, and explained, giving meaning and showing the wisdom of God, and manifesting his dispositions toward humanity, preforming the kingdom of Christ, and pre-evangelizing and pre-announcing the heritage of the holy Jerusalem, since the one who loves God will profit so much that he will even see God and hear his voice, and from hearing him be glorified so much that others cannot gaze upon the face of his glory, just as it was said by Daniel: "Those who understand will shine like the brightness of the firmament, and the many righteous like the stars forever, and still" (Daniel). Just as we have shown, then, if someone reads the Scriptures: for the Lord so instructed his disciples after his resurrection from the dead, showing them from those very Scriptures that it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to enter into his glory, and that in his name repentance for the forgiveness of sins should be preached in all the world. And the disciple will be perfected, becoming like a master of a household who brings forth from his treasure things new and old.
notes: True knowledge tied to apostles’ teaching and church succession.
latin: Si quis igitur intentus legat Scripturas, inveniet in iisdem de Christo sermonem, et nove vocationis preefigurationem, Hyc est enim thesaurus absconsus in agro, id est, in isto (Ager enim mundus est,) absconsus vero in Seripturis thesaurus Christus, quoniam per typos et parabolas significabatur, Sunde poterat hoe quod secundum hominem est intelligi, priusquam consummatio eorum quee consummata sunt veniret, quee est adventus Christi? Et propter hoe Danieli * prophet dicebatur : Muni sermones, et signa librum usque ad tempus consummationis, quoadusque discant multi, et adimpleatur agnitio. In eo enim cum~ perficietur dispersio, cognoscent omnia hac. Sed et Hieremias ait : In novissimis diebus intelligent ea. Omnis enim prophetia, priusquam habeat effectum, senigmata et ambiguitates sunt hominibus.. Cum autem venerit tempus, et evenerit quod prophetatum est, tune prophetiz habent liquidam et certam expositionem. Et topropter hoe quidem Judzeis cum legitur Lex in hoc nune tempore, fabulze similis est: non enim habent expositionem omnium rerum pertinentem ad adventum Filii Dei, qui est secundum hominem: a Christianis vero cum legitur, thesaurus est, absconsus in agro, cruce vero Christi revelatus est, et explanatus, et ditans sensum et ostendens sapientiam Dei, et eas que sunt erga hominem dispositiones ejus manifestans, et Christi regnum preformans, et heereditatem sanctze Hierusalem preeevangelisans, et preenuntians, quoniam in tantum homo diligens Deum proficiet, ut etiam videat Deum, et audiat sermonem ejus, et ex auditu ejus in tantum glorificari, uti reliqui non possint intendere in faciem glorie ejus, quemadmodum dictum est a Daniele: Quoniam intelligentes fulgebunt, quemadmodum claritas firmamenti, et a multis justis sicut stelle in secula, et adhuc. ®Quemadmodum igitur ostendimus, si quis legat Scripturas. Etenim Dominus sie disseruit discipulis post resurrectionem suam a mortuis, ex ipsis Scripturis ostendens eis, quoniam oportebat pati Christum, et intrare in gloriam suam, et in nomine ejus remissionem peccatorum predicari in toto mundo. Et erit consummatus discipulus, et similis patrifamilias qui de thesauro suo profert nova et vetera.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: It is necessary to obey the presbyters who are in the Church, those who possess succession from the Apostles, just as we have shown; for they, together with the succession of the episcopate, have received a certain charisma of truth according to the will of the Father (Leviticus 10:1-2). But those others who stand apart from the principal succession, and who gather in whatever place, must be regarded with suspicion, whether as heretics and men of bad judgment, or as those who divide, are puffed up, and please themselves, or again as hypocrites who act for the sake of gain and vain glory (Numbers 16:31-33). All these, however, are far from the truth (1 Kings 12:26-33). The heretics, bringing foreign fire to the altar of God — that is, foreign doctrines — will be consumed by heavenly fire, just as Nadab and Abihu were. Those who rise up against the truth and urge others against the Church of God remain in the underworld, swallowed by the abyss of the earth, just as Dathan and Abiram were at the cleft. But those who tear apart and separate the unity of the Church receive from God the same penalty as Jeroboam.
notes: Obey presbyters who have succession from the apostles.
latin: eis qui in Ecclesia sunt presbyteris obaudire oportet, his qui successionem habent ab Apostolis, sicut ostendimus; qui cum episcopatus successione charisma veritatis certum secundum placitum Patris acceperunt: reliquos vero qui absistunt principali successione, et quocunque loco colliguntur, suspectos habere, vel quasi hereticos et mal sententize, vel quasi scindentes et elatos et sibi placentes, aut rursus ut hypocritas, queestus gratia et vanz gloriz hoc operantes. Omnes autem hi a veritate. Et heretici quidem alienum ignem afferentes ad altare Dei, id est alienas doctrinas, a ccelesti igne comburentur, quemadmodum Nadab et Abiud. Qui vero exsurgunt contra veritatem, et alteros adhortantur adversus Eecclesiam Dei, remanent apud inferos, voragine terre absorpti, quemadmodum circa Chore Dathan et Abiron. Qui autem scindunt et separant unitatem Ecclesie, eandem quam Hieroboam pcenam percipiunt a Deo.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: Those, however, who are believed to be presbyters by many, but serve their own lusts, and, do not place the fear of God supreme in their hearts, but conduct themselves with contempt towards others, and are puffed up with the pride of holding the chief seat, and work evil deeds in secret, saying, No man sees us, shall be convicted by the Word, who does not judge after outward appearance (secundum gloriam), nor looks upon the countenance, but the heart; and they shall hear those words, to be found in Daniel the prophet:

O you seed of Canaan, and not of Judah, beauty has deceived you, and lust perverted your heart. You that are waxen old in wicked days, now your sins which you have committed aforetime have come to light; for you have pronounced false judgments, and have been accustomed to condemn the innocent, and to let the guilty go free, albeit the Lord says, The innocent and the righteous shall you not slay. Of whom also did the Lord say:

But if the evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delays his coming, and shall begin to smite the man-servants and maidens, and to eat and drink and be drunken; the lord of that servant shall come in a day that he looks not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, and shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the unbelievers.
notes: Those who leave the church and gather illicitly.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: 7. He shall also judge those who give rise to schisms, who are destitute of the love of God, and who look to their own special advantage rather than to the unity of the Church; and who for trifling reasons, or any kind of reason which occurs to them, cut in pieces and divide the great and glorious body of Christ, and so far as in them lies, [positively] destroy it — men who prate of peace while they give rise to war, and do in truth strain out a gnat, but swallow a camel.

Matthew 23:24 For no reformation of so great importance can be effected by them, as will compensate for the mischief arising from their schism. He shall also judge all those who are beyond the pale of the truth, that is, who are outside the Church; but he himself shall be judged by no one.

For to him all things are consistent: he has a full faith in one God Almighty, of whom are all things; and in the Son of God, Jesus Christ our Lord, by whom are all things, and in the dispensations connected with Him, by means of which the Son of God became man; and a firm belief in the Spirit of God, who furnishes us with a knowledge of the truth, and has set forth the dispensations of the Father and the Son, in virtue of which He dwells with every generation of men, according to the will of the Father.
notes: Disciple judges heresies; holds church’s preaching.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: Those who claim that God came into something alien, as if desiring what is foreign, are empty in their thinking. They suppose He did this to present a man made by another to a God who neither made nor founded anything, a man abandoned from the beginning by the true fashioning of humanity. The coming of such a one is not just. Nor did He truly redeem us by His blood if He was not truly made man, restoring to His own creation what was declared in the beginning. He did not snatch away what was alien through deceit; rather, He justly and kindly restores what is properly His. As far as apostasy is concerned, He justly redeems us from it by His blood; as far as we who are redeemed are concerned, He acts kindly. We gave Him nothing beforehand, nor does He desire anything from us as though He were in need. We are the ones who need communion with Him, and so He kindly poured Himself out to gather us into the Father's bosom.

Those who despise God's entire economy, deny the salvation of the flesh, and scorn its regeneration, saying it is incapable of incorruptibility, are vain in every way. For if this flesh is not saved, then the Lord did not redeem us with His blood. Neither is the cup of the Eucharist a participation in His blood, nor is the bread we break a participation in His body (1 Cor 10:16). Blood comes only from veins and flesh, and from the rest of what belongs to human substance. By that very substance the Word of God was truly made flesh and redeemed us with His blood. His Apostle also says: "In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins" (Col 1:14). Since we are His members and are nourished through creation, He Himself provides that creation for us — making His sun rise and sending rain as He wills. The cup, which comes from creation, He made His own blood poured out, by which our blood is increased. The bread, which comes from creation, He confirmed as His own body, by which our bodies are increased. When the mixed cup and the baked bread receive the Word of God, they become the Eucharist of the blood and body of Christ, from which the substance of our flesh is increased and sustained. How then can they deny that flesh is capable of receiving God's gift, which is eternal life — flesh that is nourished by the blood and body of Christ and is a member of Him? The blessed Apostle says in the letter to the Ephesians: "We are members of His body, of His flesh and of His bones" (Eph 5:30). He does not say this of some spiritual, invisible man — for the Spirit has neither bones nor flesh — but of that constitution which belongs to the true human being, consisting of flesh, nerves, and bones. This constitution is nourished from the cup which is His blood, and increased from the bread which is His body.

Just as a vine shoot planted in the earth bears fruit in its season, and a grain of wheat falling into the earth, dissolved, rises multiplied by the Spirit of God who contains all things — and these then, through wisdom, come into human use, and receiving the Word of God become the Eucharist, which is the body and blood of Christ — so also our bodies, nourished by it, laid in the earth and dissolved there, will rise again in their season. The Word of God gives them resurrection, to the glory of God the Father, who clothes this mortal with immortality and freely gives incorruptibility to the corruptible. For God's power is perfected in weakness (2 Cor 12:9). This is so that we, not having life from ourselves, may not at some time be puffed up against God, harboring an ungrateful mind. Rather, learning by experience, we know that we have perseverance for eternity from His greatness, not our own. Thus we are not deprived of the glory that surrounds God as it truly is, nor do we ignore our own nature. Instead we come to know what God can do and what man receives as a benefit, so that we never stray from the true understanding of what things are and how they are — that is, of God and of man. Or did God perhaps become dissolution in us for this very reason: that, instructed through all things, we might be diligent in all things, neither ignorant of God nor of ourselves?
notes: Eucharist: earthly bread receives Word; cup/body realism — mark carefully.
latin: Vanr autem et qui in aliena dicunt Deum venisse, velut aliena concupiscentem, uti eum hominem qui ab altero factus esset exhiberet ei Deo, qui neque fecisset neque condidisset, sed et ? qui desolatus esset ab initio a propria hominum fabricatione. Non justus adventus ejus qui secundum eos %adyenit in aliena; neque vere nos redemit sanguine suo, si non vere homo factus est, restaurans suo plasmati quod dictum est in principio, factum aliena in dolo diripiens, sed sua propria juste et benigne assuquantum attinet quidem ad apostasiam, juste suo sanguine redimens nos ab ea; quantum autem ad nos, qui redemti sumus, benigne. Nihil enim illi ante dedimus, neque desiderat aliquid a nobis, quasi indigens ; nos autem indigemus ejus que est ad eum communionis: et propterea benigne effudit semetipsum, ut nos colligeret in sinum Patris. * Vani autem omnimodo, qui universam dispositionem Dei contemnunt, et carnis salutem negant et regenerationem ejus spernunt, dicentes non eam capacem esse incorruptibilitatis. 4Si autem non salvetur heee nec Dominus sanguine suo redemit nos, neque calix Eucharistize communicatio sanguinis ejus est, neque panis quem frangimus communicatio corporis ejus est.* Sanguis enim non est nisi a venis et carnibus, et a reliqua quze est secundum hominem substantia, qua vere factum Verbum Dei, sanguine suo redemit nos. Quemadmodum et Apostolus ejus ait: In quo habemus redemtionem per sanguinem ejus, et remissionem peccaTpepouedar Tv de 2. Et quoniam membra ejus sumus, et per creaturam nutrimur; creaturam autem ipse nobis prestat, solem suum oriri faciens, et pluens quemadmodum vult, eum calicem qui est creatura, suum sanguinem qui effusus est, ex quo auget nostrum sanguinem ; et eum panem qui est a creatura, suum corpus confirmavit, ex quo nostra auget corpora. Quando ergo et mixtus calix, et factus panis percipit Verbum Dei, et fit Eucharistia sanguinis et corporis Christi, ex quibus augetur et consistit carnis nostree substantia ; quomodo carnem negant capacem esse donationis Dei, quee est vita eterna, quee sanguine et corpore Christi nutritur, et membrum ejus est? Quemadmodum et beatus A postolus ait in epistola que est ad Ephesios; Quoniam membra sumus corporis ejus, de carne ejus, et de ossibus ejus: non de spiritali aliquo et invisibili homine dicens heec; (Spiritus enim neque ossa, neque carnes habet) sed de ea dispositione, quee est secundum ? verum hominem, que ex carnibus et nervis et ossibus consistit ; quae de calice, qui est sanguis ejus, nutritur; et de pane, quod est corpus ejus, augetur. 3. Et quemadmodum lignum yitis depositum in terram, suo fructificat tempore, et granum tritici decidens in terram et dissolutum, multiplex surgit per Spiritum Dei, qui continet omnia ; quee deinde per sapientiam in usum ‘ hominis yeniunt, et percipientia verbum Dei Eucharistia fiunt, quod est corpus et sanguis Christi: sic et nostra corpora ex ea nutrita, et reposita in terram, et resoluta in ea, resurgent in suo tempore, Verbo Dei resurrectionem eis donante, in gloriam Dei Patris: qui huic mortali immortalitatem cireumdat, et corruptibili incorruptelam gratuito donat, quoniam virtus Dei in infirmitate perficitur: ut non quasi ex nobisipsis habentes vitam, inflemur aliquando et extollamur adversus Deum, ingratam mentem accipientes; experimento Tautem discentes, quoniam ex illius magnitudine, et non ex nostra habemus in zeternum perseverantiam, neque ab ea que est circa § Deum gloria, sicuti est, frustremur aliquando, neque nostram naturam ignoremus ; sed ut sciamus, et quid Deus potest, et quid homo beneficii accipit: et non erremus aliquando a vera comprehensione eorum qu sunt, et quemadmodum sunt, id est Dei et Et numquid forte, quaemadmodum preediximus, propter hoe passus est Deus fieri in nobis resolutionem; ut per omnia eruditi, in omnibus simus diligentes, neque Deum, neque nosmetipsos ignorantes ?

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: The prophets make it perfectly clear that God commanded certain observances in the law not because He needs our service, but for our own sake. The Lord has taught the same truth just as plainly: He does not need our offerings, but accepts them for the sake of the one who offers them. When He saw His people neglecting justice and turning away from the love of God, yet imagining they could appease Him through sacrifices and other ceremonial observances, Samuel told them: "God does not want burnt offerings and sacrifices, but wants you to listen to His voice. Obedience is better than sacrifice, and to listen is better than the fat of rams" (1 Sam 15:22). David says the same: "You did not want sacrifice and offering, but You have given me an open ear. You did not ask for burnt offerings and sin offerings" (Ps 40:6). He was teaching them that God desires obedience, which saves them, rather than sacrifices and burnt offerings, which do nothing to make them just—and in saying this he was also prophesying the New Testament. The fiftieth Psalm states this even more clearly: "If You had wanted sacrifice, I would have given it; You take no delight in burnt offerings. The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, You will not despise" (Ps 51:16-17). Since God needs nothing, the preceding Psalm declares: "I will not accept a bull from your house, or goats from your folds. For every beast of the forest is Mine, the cattle on a thousand hills. I know all the birds of the air, and all that moves in the field is Mine. If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world and its fullness are Mine. Do I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?" (Ps 50:9-13). Then, so that no one would think He rejects these things out of anger, He gives them counsel: "Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High. Call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you shall glorify Me" (Ps 50:14-15). He rejects the very things by which sinners thought they could appease Him, showing that He needs nothing; but He urges and admonishes them toward the things by which a person is justified and draws near to God. Isaiah says the same: "What to Me is the multitude of your sacrifices? says the Lord; I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed beasts" (Is 1:11). After rejecting burnt offerings, sacrifices, grain offerings, new moons, Sabbaths, festivals, and the whole train of observances that follow them, He points them to what truly saves: "Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your deeds from before My eyes; cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; bring justice to the fatherless, plead the widow's cause. Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord" (Is 1:16-18). He does not turn away their sacrifices like a man moved by emotion, as many dare to claim, but in mercy toward their misguided zeal He points them to the true sacrifice—one which, when offered, propitiates God so that they may receive life from Him.
notes: New covenant sacrifice / eucharist offering language — mark carefully.
latin: Quonram autem non indigens Deus servitute eorum, sed propter ipsos quasdam observantias in lege praeceperit, plenissime prophetz indicant. Et rursus quoniam non indiget Deus oblatione eorum, sed propter ipsum qui offerat hominem, manifeste Dominus docuit, quemadmodum ostendimus. Si quando enim negligentes eos justitiam, et abstinentes a dilectione Dei videbat, per sacrificia autem et reliquas typicas observantias putantes propitiari Deum, dicebat eis Samuel quidem sic; Non vult Deus holocausta et sacrificia, sed vult exaudiri vocem suam. Ecce, auditus bonus super sacrificium, et auditus super adipem arietum. David autem ait: Sacrificium et oblationem noluisti ; ®aures autem perfecisti mihi: holocausta etiam pro delicto non postulasti. Docens eos quoniam obauditionem vult Deus, que servat eos, quam sacrificia et holocaustomata, que nihil eis prosunt ad justitiam : et novum simul prophetans Testamentum. Manifestius autem adhue in quinquagesimo Psalmo de his ait: Quoniam si voluisses sacrificium, dedissem utique: holocaustis non delectaberis. Sacrificiwm Deo spiritus contribulatus Quoniam ergo nihil et humiliatum Dominus non despernet. indiget Deus, in eo qui est ante hune Psalmo ait: Non accipiam de domo tua vitulos, nec de gregibus tuis hircos. sunt omnes bestiw terra, jumenta in montibus et boves; cognovi omnia volatilia coli, et species agri mecum est. dicam tibi : meus est enim orbis terra, et plenitudo ejus. Nunquid manducabo carnes taurorum, aut sanguinem hircorum potabo? Deinde ne quis putet, propterea quod irasceretur, eum recusare infert, consilium ei dans: Jmmola Deo sacrificium laudis, et redde Altissimo vota tua, et invoca me in die tribulationis tuce, et eripiam te, et glorificabis me; illa quidem per que putabant peccantes propitiari Deum abnuens, et ostendens quod ipse nullius rei indiget ; ®heee autem per que justificatur homo, et appropinDeo, hortatur et admonet. 2. Hoc idem autem et Esaias ait: Quo mihi multitudinem sacrificiorum vestrorum, dicit Dominus? Plenus sum. Et cum abnuisset holocaustomata, et sacrificia, et oblationes, et adhuc neomenias, et sabbata, et ferias, et reliquam universam consequentem his observationem, intulit, suadens eis que salutaria sunt: Lavamini, mundi estote, auferte nequitias a cordibus. vestris ab oculis meis: desinite a malitiis vestris, discite bonum facere, exquirite judicium, eruite eum qui injuriam patitur, judicate pupillo, et justificate viduam, et venite disputemus, dicit Dominus. Non enim sicut homo motus, ut multi audent dicere, divertit eorum sacrificia; sed miserans eorum cexcitati, et verum sacrificium insinuans, quod offerentes propitiabuntur Deum, ut ab eo vitam percipiant.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: The Church's offering, which the Lord commanded to be offered throughout the world, is regarded as a pure sacrifice before God and is accepted by Him; God does not need a sacrifice from us, but the one who offers is glorified in the very act of offering, provided his gift is accepted.

Gifts presented to a king demonstrate honor and affection, and the Lord, desiring us to offer in all simplicity and innocence, taught this when He said: when you bring your gift to the altar and remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, go first and be reconciled to your brother, and then return to offer your gift (Matthew 5:23-24).

We must therefore offer God the firstfruits of His creation, just as Moses also says: you shall not appear empty-handed before the presence of the Lord your God (Deuteronomy 16:16); thus the person who shows gratitude in these things is deemed worthy, and the one who comes from God receives honor.

It is not the kind of offerings that is rejected, for there were offerings then and there are offerings now: sacrifices among the people of old, sacrifices also in the Church; but the form has changed, since now the offering is made not by slaves but by free people.
There is one and the same Lord, yet the character of a slave's offering is distinct from that of a free person's, so that through our offerings the sign of freedom is displayed.

Nothing with Him is idle, without a sign, or without meaning; for this reason those of old had their tithes consecrated, but those who have received freedom set aside what is theirs for the Lord's purposes, giving cheerfully and freely not lesser things but rather with hope of greater things, like that widow and this poor person who cast their entire livelihood into the treasury of God.

From the beginning God looked with favor on Abel's gifts, because he offered with simplicity and justice, but He did not look on Cain's sacrifice, for he harbored zeal and malice against his brother and division in his heart; God, exposing his hidden thoughts, said: 'Have you not sinned, if you offer correctly but do not divide correctly? Be still; for God is not pleased by sacrifice.'
notes: New covenant sacrifice / eucharist offering language — mark carefully.
latin: Ierrur Ecclesiz oblatio, quam Dominus doeuit offerri in universo mundo, purum sacrificium reputatum est apud Deum, et acceptum est ei: non quod indigeat a nobis sacrificium, sed quoniam is qui offert, glorificatur ipse in eo quod offert, si acceptetur munus ejus. Per musus enim erga regem, et honos, et affectio ostenditur: quod in omni simplicitate et innocentia Dominus volens nos offerre, preedicavit dicens: Cwm igitur offers munus tuum ad altare, et recordatus fueris, quoniam frater twus habet aliquid adversum te, dimitte munus tuum ante altare, et vade primum reconciliari fratri tuo, et tune reversus offeres munus tuum. Offerre igitur oportet Deo primitias ejus creature, sicut et Moyses ait: Non apparebis vacuus ante conspectum Domini Dei tui ; ut in gratus exstitit homo, in his gratus eis deputatus, eum qui est ab eo percipiat honorem. Et non genus oblationum reprobatum est; oblationes enim et illic, oblationes autem et hic: sacrificia in populo, sacrificia et in Ecclesia : sed species immutata est tantum, quippe cum jam non a servis, sed a liberis offeratur. Unus enim et idem Dominus; proprium autem character servilis oblationis, et proprium liberorum, uti et per oblationes ostendatur indicium libertatis. excerpts.author: Lactantius
english: When he had set in order for his disciples the preaching of the gospel and of his name, a cloud suddenly wrapped around him and lifted him into heaven on the fortieth day after the passion, as Daniel had shown it would be, saying: “And behold, coming in the clouds of heaven as a son of man, and he came unto the Ancient of Days.” The disciples, scattered through the provinces, laid the foundations of the church everywhere, themselves also doing great and almost unbelievable miracles in the name of their Master, God—because as he departed he had equipped them with power and authority, so that the account of the new announcement could be founded and confirmed.

He also opened to them all things to come: which Peter and Paul preached at Rome, and that preaching has remained written in memory. In it, among many other wonders, they also said this would happen: that after a short time God would send a king who would overthrow the Jews and level their cities to the ground, and besiege them worn out by hunger and thirst. Then they would eat the bodies of their own and consume one another; at last they would come captive into the hands of enemies and see their wives most bitterly mistreated before their eyes, virgins violated and prostituted, boys carried off, little ones dashed down, everything wasted by fire and sword, captives forever driven from their lands—because they had exulted over the most beloved and approved Son of God. And so after their death, when Nero had killed them, Vespasian extinguished the name and nation of the Jews and did all that they had foretold would come.

latin: Ordinata uero discipulis suis euangelii ac nominis sui praedicatione circumfudit se repente nubes eumque in caelum sustulit, quadragesimo post passionem die, sicut Daniel fore ostenderat dicens: et ecce in nubibus caeli ut filius hominis ueniens (et) usque ad uetustum dierum peruenit. discipuli uero per prouincias dispersi fundamenta ecclesiae ubique posuerunt facientes et ipsi in nomine magistri dei magna et paene incredibilia miracula, quia discedens instruxerat eos uirtute ac potestate, quo posset nouae adnuntiationis ratio fundari et confirmari. sed et futura illis aperuit omnia: quae Petrus et Paulus Romae praedicauerunt et ea praedicatio in memoriam scripta permansit. in qua cum multa alia mira tum etiam hoc futurum esse dixerunt, ut post breue tempus inmitteret deus regem, qui expugnaret Iudaeos et ciuitates eorum solo adaequaret, ipsos autem fame sitique confectos obsideret. tum fore ut corporibus suorum uescerentur et consumerent inuicem, postremo ut capti uenirent in manus hostium et in conspectu suo uexari acerbissime coniuges suas cernerent, uiolari ac prostitui uirgines, diripi pueros, allidi paruulos, omnia denique igni ferroque uastari, captiuos in perpetuum terris suis exterminari, eo quod exultauerint super amantissimum et probatissimum dei filium. itaque post illorum obitum, cum eos Nero interemisset, Iudaeorum nomen et gentem Vespasianus extinxit fecitque omnia quae illi futura praedixerant.

excerpts.author: Lactantius
english: But since many heresies have arisen and by the instigation of demons the people of God has been split, the truth must be briefly determined for us and set in its own proper dwelling, so that if anyone desires to draw the water of life he is not led to worn-out cisterns that have no spring, but knows God’s richest fountain, by which irrigated he may drink perennial light. Before all things it befits us to know that both he himself and his ambassadors foretold that very many sects would arise which would break the concord of the holy body, and warned that we should beware with the highest prudence lest we ever fall into the snares and frauds of that adversary of ours with whom God has willed us to wrestle; then that he gave sure commands which we ought to keep forever. Most, forgetful of these, deserted the heavenly road and built for themselves deviant paths through bends and precipices, by which they might lead an unwary and simple part of the people to darkness and death.

How that happened I will set out. There were some of ours—either less firm in faith, or less taught, or less cautious—who made a split of unity and scattered the church. But those whose faith was slippery, while they pretended to know and worship God, aiming at increasing wealth and honor, were grasping after the highest priesthood. Beaten by stronger men, they preferred to withdraw with their supporters rather than endure as superiors those whom they themselves had coveted to outrank. Some, not well enough trained in the heavenly letters, when they could not answer truth’s accusers—who objected that it was impossible or unfit that God should shut himself in a woman’s womb, or that heavenly majesty could be brought down to such weakness as to be contempt, mockery, insult, and sport to humans, and at last even endure torments and be fixed to the abominable gibbet—were warped from the straight road and corrupted the heavenly letters, so that they might compose a new teaching for themselves without any root or stability. Others, drawn by the prophecy of false prophets, of whom both the true prophets and he himself had foretold, fell away from God’s teaching and left the true tradition. But all those, caught in demonic frauds which they ought to have foreseen and avoided, lost the divine name and worship through imprudence. For when they are called Phrygians or Novatians or Valentinians or Marcionites or Anthropians or any others, they have ceased to be Christians—having lost Christ’s name, they have put on human and foreign titles.

Therefore only the catholic church is the one that retains the true worship. This is the fountain of truth, this the dwelling of faith, this the temple of God: if anyone has not entered it, or if anyone has gone out from it, he is alien from the hope of life and salvation. No one ought to flatter himself with stubborn dispute. For it is about life and salvation: unless it is looked after carefully and diligently, it will be lost and extinguished. Yet because each and every gathering of heretics thinks itself especially Christian and its own to be the catholic church, one must know that that is the true one in which there is confession and repentance, which healthfully cures the sins and wounds to which the weakness of the flesh is subject. I have reported these things for now in a few words by way of warning, lest anyone, desiring to flee error, be entangled in a greater error while he does not know the inner shrine of truth. Afterward we will fight more fully and richly against all the sects of lies in a work of its own. It follows that, since we have spoken enough of true religion and wisdom, in the next book we should treat of justice.

latin: Sed quoniam multae haereses extiterunt et instinctibus daemonum populus dei scissus est, determinanda est nobis ueritas breuiter et in suo proprio domicilio conlocanda, ut si quis aquam uitae cupiet haurire, non ad detritos lacus deferatur qui non habent uenam, sed uberrimum dei nouerit fontem quo inrigatus perenni luce potiatur. ante omnia scire nos conuenit et ipsum et legatos eius praedixisse quod plurimae sectae haberent exsistere quae concordiam sancti corporis rumperent, ac monuisse ut summa prudentia caueremus, ne quando in laqueos et fraudes illius aduersarii nostri cum quo nos luctari deus uoluit incideremus; tum dedisse certa mandata, quae in perpetuum custodire debemus: quorum plerique immemores deserto itinere caelesti uias sibi deuias per anfractus et praecipitia condiderunt, per quas partem plebis incautam et simplicem ad tenebras mortemque deducerent. quod quatenus acciderit exponam.

fuerunt quidam nostrorum uel minus stabilita fide uel minus docti uel minus cauti, qui discidium facerent unitatis et ecclesiam dissiparent. sed ii quorum fides fuit lubrica, cum deum nosse se et colere simularent, augendis opibus et honori studentes adfectabant maximum sacerdotium. et a potioribus uicti secedere cum suffragatoribus suis maluerunt quam eos ferre praepositos quibus concupierant ipsi ante praeponi. quidam uero non satis caelestibus litteris eruditi cum ueritatis accusatoribus respondere non possent, obicientibus uel inpossibile uel incongruens esse ut deus in uterum se mulieris includeret nec caelestem illam maiestatem ad tantam infirmitatem potuisse deduci, ut hominibus contemtui derisui contumeliae ludibrio esset, postremo etiam cruciamenta perferret atque exsecrabili patibulo figeretur, quae omnia cum neque ingenio neque doctrina defendere ac refutare possent — nec enim uim rationemque penitus peruidebant —, deprauati sunt ab itinere recto et caelestes litteras corruperunt, ut nouam sibi doctrinam sine ulla. radice ac stabilitate conponerent. nonnulli autem falsorum prophetarum uaticinio inlecti, de quibus et ueri prophetae et ipse praedixerat, exciderunt a doctrina dei et traditionem ueram reliquerunt. sed illi omnes daemonicis fraudibus inretiti, quas prospicere et cauere debuerant, diuinum nomen et cultum per inprudentiam perdiderunt. cum enim Phryges aut Nouatiani aut Valentiniani aut Marcionitae aut Anthropiani seu quilibet alii nominantur, Christiani esse desierunt, qui Christi nomine amisso humana et externa uocabula induerunt.

sola igitur catholica ecclesia est quae uerum cultum retinet. hic est fons ueritatis, hoc domicilium fidei, hoc templum dei: quo si quis non intrauerit uel a quo si quis exierit, a spe uitae ac salutis alienus est. neminem sibi oportet pertinaci concertatione blandiri. agitur enim de uita et salute: cui nisi caute ac diligenter consulatur, amissa et extincta erit. sed tamen quia singuli quique coetus haereticorum se potissimum Christianos et suam esse catholicam ecclesiam putant, sciendum est illam esse ueram in qua est confessio et paenitentia, quae peccata et uulnera quibus subiecta est inbecillitas carnis salubriter curat. haec interim paucis admonendi gratia rettuli, ne quis errorem fugere cupiens maiore inplicetur errore, dum penetrale ueritatis ignorat: postea plenius et uberius contra omnes mendaciorum sectas proprio separatoque opere pugnabimus. Sequitur ut quoniam satis de religione uera et sapientia locuti sumus, in proximo libro de iustitia disseramus.
